thread.label: Genesis 1:25
thread.text: And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

classes.title: My Temple My Choice

precepts.label: Leviticus 11:44
precepts.why:
Many of our people who believe Christ is black and believe they are Israelites still struggle with Paul’s words: “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving”. They take it to mean, just pray over it and eat whatever you want. But what makes every creature good? “And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good for its purpose. Worms are one of the best ways to prepare land for planting, but we do not eat worms. Pigs were the garbage disposal, because they eat everything. Can you pray over a human foot and eat it?

The bottom feeders have a purpose too. Catfish, loaches, shrimp and snails are sold as natural tank cleaners: they eat the uneaten food, the algae and the waste. Put crab or any bottom feeder in murky water and in a few hours it will be clear. The filter you change in a fish tank is what you eat when you eat shrimp; that is why they are called the roaches of the sea. Lobster was once fed to prisoners. And pork carries the trichinella worm, which can travel into the muscles and even the brain. If a creature’s job is to eat garbage, what will it do to you? Gout, high cholesterol, hypertension, even lost fingers and feet.

Read the verse before and the verse after. The meats are “received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and “thy law is the truth.” To believe is to keep the law: “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” And the creature “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Christians never read that far.

So where does the word of God sanctify the animals? Here: “ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He says it twice: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” And how are we holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.”

“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” You move like a flash when something comes at your eye; flee from sin that fast. John says, “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food, and overeating, is destroying the temple the Most High gave you to do his work. He wants a fit army: you cannot teach discipline in the street without having it yourself, and you cannot go to camp and become a liability.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears
Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.label: Psalms 17:15
precepts.why:
Men, we want dominion. We want rulership; we want to subdue the nations. God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion,” and he told them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.” Being made after his image, we were supposed to subdue the earth and bring everything under foot.

When you read “after our likeness,” understand it is more than what you look like. At that time everybody was of color, yet God gave a specific people rulership. David shows what the likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is not just appearance; it is being righteous. Christ is black, God is black, and we are made after his image, but the image alone does not bring the dominion. In being righteous we will subdue and have dominion over things.

So the government must be in place, and in that we must be keeping the commandments. It is the only way we are going to get it. That government cannot happen unless we are righteous.

precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”. God's image is the greatest image there is, and he mirrored man after himself, then gave him dominion and rulership. “And God blessed them”. But the blessing did not end with his image and dominion. In chapter 2, “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.”

The breath of life is wisdom, and it is what activated us. The word of God has to activate your life. God gave us laws to govern us so that we could be that special people; without them we would be just like every other nation. We are at the lowest state right now because we sinned against God, but we do not want to share power with any nation or be all-inclusive. God wants all or none, and we wait in this state until he puts us back in our rightful place.

Wisdom of Solomon 7 shows what that breath is. Wisdom, “which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit”. That is why we understand the Bible and have a scripture for everything we say. She is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things”. Free from care means free from the cares of this world. Mark 4 names them: “the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” Wisdom says beware of covetousness, so you do not entertain it.

Then the verse that ties it to Genesis 2: “For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Wisdom flows down from the Almighty and molds you, so if she is influencing you, you are tethered to God. Otherwise something else, covetousness or lust, is influencing you. That breath is what God gave us in Genesis 2, and we let something else draw us away. God gave us everything, and we were led away by women, money, riches and cars, as if the things he created were greater than him.

The power of God is his word. Hebrews 4 says “the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword”, the same words used of wisdom, and it “is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” Psalms 19 names the pure influence: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” “the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” We were once simple; now wisdom makes us wise and we see clearly. In 1 Samuel 10:6 the Spirit of the Lord comes and a man is “turned into another man.”

Much is given, so much is required. Christ asks, “why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” The one who hears and does is like the man who “laid the foundation on a rock”, and that foundation lets you endure tribulation; the one who hears and does not is the house that falls. Learn yourself before chasing deep prophecy: get off the sin first. Wisdom is “the unspotted mirror of the power of God”, and James says pure religion is “to keep himself unspotted from the world.” “remaining in herself, she maketh all things new”. Tether yourself to wisdom and she makes you new.

People are watching. A sister came to the truth because she saw the camp in the streets and not one brother tried to talk to her. That is the right example: a people made in God's image, living by the breath he gave, set apart from every other nation.

classes.title: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.label: Matthew 4:1
precepts.why:
“And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?” Where are you, Adam? I put you down here to rule this earth, and now I'm looking for you. “And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked”. He was afraid because he knew he had messed up. Naked means exposed to sin. They were not running around without clothes; they were never supposed to have the knowledge of sin, and now sin was in them. And Satan showed it to Eve first.

To show what Satan did, the class read how he tempted Christ, from Luke 4. Christ was “led by the Spirit into the wilderness, Being forty days tempted of the devil.” That is what brothers are going to go through: you will be tempted, and a man is supposed to be able to resist temptation. Women are not as strong as men, which is why she is supposed to look up to you. Christ resisted.

First the bread: “If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread.” You have the power, so why sit here hungry? It was an attempt to make Christ forget why he was fasting, the way a cupboard full of food tempts you to forget your purpose. “It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.” Women will forget the course they are on, and that is why men have to protect her. She is in serious trouble without a husband.

Then Satan raised the stakes: “And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” That is what Satan did to Eve. He likely hit her several times while she resisted, and then showed her something greater: you do not have to be under your husband; a time will come when you will be over him. He showed her America, with the man serving her, selling drugs for her, committing crimes for her, worshipping her. She spiritually fornicated with Satan, and brought it back to Adam with her beauty, without telling him about the death, and he took the bait.

When the reckoning came, Adam blamed her: “The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.” It was not her fault; God put him over her, and Adam did not have to listen. Then she blamed the serpent: “The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.” The family unit was attacked. The family is the backbone of the nation, and once husband and wife violate each other's roles they work against each other instead of for each other, and the children come out confused and troubled. That destruction came down through the generations to husbands and wives today. Men must restore the order and bring back our civility.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 2:5
precepts.why:
God told Noah, “Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.” Why was Noah chosen to be delivered with his family? Peter explains it: God “spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”.

The old world is the world we read about in Genesis 7, and God did not spare it: he killed all flesh. Noah was righteous because he preached righteousness and kept the commandments. He was a godly man in an ungodly world, and he had received his orders from God on exactly how to build the ark and did it faithfully. His standing up for God is what brought the flood in upon the ungodly.

Why is he called the eighth person? The other seven were his wife, his three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, and their wives. Noah is counted eighth because a true captain, a true leader, made sure his wife, his sons and their wives were on first, and he was the last one to get on the ark. When Noah gave the word, they did not question him; they got on.

That is why men of God have to be strong. We come to the Sabbath because we are sick. We are surrounded by the world all week and fighting the sin around us and in our own thoughts, so we need to be around brothers and sisters who will correct us in righteousness.

The flood shows the mind of God for destruction. Nobody was righteous except the ones on the ark. The coming destruction, a thermonuclear war, will be on another level, and we want to be spiritually the men and women in that ark, not the ones drowning. A lot more than eight will make it this time, but very few, so do not be surprised when your family does not listen. Keep the commandments, preach righteousness, and God will deliver us.

precepts.label: Luke 17:32
precepts.why:
The angels pulled Lot into the house and smote the men at the door with blindness, and even blinded they wearied themselves trying to find the door. Then the angels took Lot out and gave them one order as the cities burned: don't look back. “And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.” “But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.”

Why would she look back? The city was being destroyed; she had just seen what happened in front of her house. She should have been glad to escape. Somebody was not vexed with the filthy conversation of that city; there was something in it she missed. That is why Luke also says, if you put your hand on the plow and look back, you are not worthy.

Christ said it in three words: “Remember Lot’s wife.” That is a warning for all of us: don't look back. You are in this truth now. Stop worrying about the long-lost cousin and auntie, stop trying to be friends with everybody and please people, stop dropping by the house on their birthday. Focus on this truth and stay away from filthiness, or be destroyed just as Lot's wife was destroyed.

Judgment is coming to Esau, as Sodom's came. “Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” We have to come out of her mentally, come back to the law, statutes and commandments, stop playing around in the truth, and keep the faith of Christ, without looking back.

precepts.label: Proverbs 3:1-5
precepts.why:
“The Lord is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God”. He will guide us. Many of us choose the ways of the world to guide us: the job guides you, the children guide you. But each of us has to walk a path, some of us start to go off it, and we have to seek good and not evil. Proverbs 3 shows what his guiding looks like.

“My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments”. Whose law? God's laws. Your heart is your mind. You have to learn the laws and keep the commandments, and that proves the laws are the commandments. “For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee”. You want to live long? Despite all these wars, rumors of wars and mayhem throughout the world, you want peace? Do what he said.

“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding”. Trust that the prophecies have to go in order. Iran is not going to bring in World War III; Iran will help unite the Arabs, and you are seeing it. And lean not on your own understanding: in the Christian church some of us used to say we're already saved. No, that's not the understanding. He that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved, and we don't know when that end is coming. So we keep enduring, keeping the commandments, seeking the good and not the evil. “In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths”.

That is how the Lord becomes our salvation in Exodus 15:2: trust in him, endure to the end, and do his commandments. Then the habitation we prepare him is the kingdom, where we have power and rule and every wrong done to us is turned upside down, not the pie-in-the-sky fairy tale of modern Christianity. The Lord is a man of war, and he is using these nations to bring a final battle. I pray I make it, and I pray you make it.

thread.label: Exodus 15:3-7
thread.text: The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.

classes.title: The God Of War & Salvation

precepts.label: Isaiah 31:1-2
precepts.why:
The Lord is a man of war, and his vengeance is on all the nations read in Psalms 83; he has a big payback coming for all of them. Egypt is one example. Exodus 15 says “Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea”, and Isaiah 31 shows what all that power was worth: “Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong”.

Did the power help them? No. All their chariots and all their war materials did not help them at all. And “they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the Lord!” We did not look to the Holy One of Israel, to our God, to save us. The God of Israel is the only God that is going to save us out of all this foolishness. The wars are going to come to the point where thermonuclear ICBMs are put in full effect and a lot of people die, and the question to ask yourself is, will it be us?

“Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words”. He is not calling back his word. Evil is set for all these nations, and these nations will be destroyed. Where will you be? You cannot have God to trust in and Christ coming to save you while you sit in confederacy with all these nations, thinking all nations are going to be saved and we are all together. That is not the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

So the right hand that “hath dashed in pieces the enemy” in Exodus 15:6 is the same hand that will overthrow every nation Israel trusts in instead of him.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 51:13-14
precepts.why:
Prophecy is coming to pass and there is no stopping it. The wild and crazy ones made demands to the proud one: not only fall back out of our country, but pay us back for all the destruction. The proud man says no, we are not going to do that. Even while they talk about peace talks, God has them in the trick bag.

“O thou that dwellest upon many waters”: that is New Babylon, America. She is “abundant in treasures”: rich from all the nations, because they have taken all the land and all the resources and oppressed all the people. And “thine end is come, and the measure of thy covetousness.” The Most High is already telling her that her end is come and it is time to step down. She is not going to step down, so God is going to put her down.

“The Lord of hosts hath sworn by himself”: the same Lord of hosts who is a man of war in Exodus 15:3. “Surely I will fill thee with men, as with caterpillers; and they shall lift up a shout against thee.” Those caterpillars are the wild and crazy ones.

If proud Babylon gives in to the demands, she loses her sovereignty over the economy, and that is her downfall. Because she is prideful and already in power, she will not do it, so it leads to war, and God activates the caterpillars. Either way it goes to war. As the Lord cast Pharaoh's chariots into the sea, he will consume this enemy as stubble.

precepts.label: Proverbs 30:7-9
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.” To see what that means, go to Proverbs.

“Two things have I required of thee; deny me them not before I die: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.”

Lest I be full and deny thee: that is one way of taking his name in vain. Lest I be poor and steal: that is sin, and sinning while bearing his name is taking the name of my God in vain. We are called by his name; he says we are a holy people, and he put his spirit in us.

So when they say you cannot keep the commandments, why can’t we? That does not mean we have never sinned. All men have sinned, and if anybody says they have not sinned, they lie. But when they say you cannot keep the commandments, it is because they want to remain in their sins.

This sits inside the first four commandments, which go into loving the Lord thy God. All of this blending of religions is meant to take you away from serving him and to keep you in sin.

thread.label: Leviticus 12:1-8
thread.text: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

classes.title: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.label: Luke 2:21-24
precepts.why:
In Acts 15 certain men came down from Judea and taught, “Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” Why does it say after the manner of Moses and not just circumcision? Leviticus 12 shows the manner of Moses. A woman who “conceived seed, and born a man child” is unclean seven days; “in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised”; she continues in the blood of her purifying thirty-three more days, forty in all for a boy and eighty for a girl. When the days are fulfilled she brings a lamb and a pigeon or turtledove for a burnt offering and a sin offering, and if she cannot afford a lamb, “two turtles, or two young pigeons”. The priest makes the atonement, and the offering covers the child as well as the mother.

Luke 2 confirms it with Mary and Christ. Mary conceived seed and bore a man child. “And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.” That is the eighth day of Leviticus 12.

“And when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord”, because “Every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord”. Then comes the offering: “to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.” Those are the offerings Leviticus 12:8 names.

So behind circumcision after the manner of Moses comes sacrifice. It is circumcision with the eighth day, the days of purifying and the offering for the woman and the child all tied together. That is what the men from Judea were pressing on the Gentiles, and that is why the scripture calls it the manner of Moses.

precepts.label: John 7:22
precepts.why:
If circumcision after the manner of Moses is circumcision with sacrifice, is all circumcision of Moses? Christ answers it: “Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man.”

Moses gave it to them, but circumcision is not of Moses. It is of the fathers, of Abraham, who was the one first circumcised. So when Acts 15 says circumcised after the manner of Moses, that is not the same thing as the circumcision of Abraham.

There are two different things here: circumcision of the fathers, and circumcision after the manner of Moses with the sacrifice of Leviticus 12 behind it. Seeing that difference is what opens up what the Pharisees were demanding and what Paul was fighting in his letters.

precepts.label: Genesis 17:24-25
precepts.why:
“And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.” “And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.”

Abraham was not circumcised on the eighth day after he was born; he was ninety-nine. Ishmael was thirteen. There was no eighth day, no days of purifying and no sacrifice. That is circumcision of the fathers, not circumcision after the manner of Moses.

The Pharisees wanted circumcision and sacrifice together, after the manner of Moses, because sacrificing was their bread and butter. As more people followed Christ, more of them stopped sacrificing, and if the people stop sacrificing, the Pharisees cannot eat. So they went into the churches saying you have to be circumcised to be saved. That is not what the Bible, Christ or the apostles taught. They were trying to put back on the people the yoke that could not be borne, the same one Peter asked about: “why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?”

precepts.label: Genesis 21:1-5
precepts.why:
“And the Lord visited Sarah as he had said”, and “Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.” Sarah conceived in old age and Abraham named the child Isaac. Then: “And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac being eight days old, as God had commanded him.” “And Abraham was an hundred years old, when his son Isaac was born unto him.”

Isaac was circumcised on the eighth day, as God commanded, but this was long before Moses. There is no reading of them going and sacrificing animals for it. So even eighth-day circumcision here is not after the manner of Moses. There is circumcision of the fathers, and there is circumcision after the manner of Moses, which carries the sacrifice.

That is how Paul can say in Galatians 5, “if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.” He means circumcised after the manner of Moses, back under the yoke of bondage, taught by the Pharisees that you must be circumcised and sacrifice an animal to be saved. “For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.” Once the temple was destroyed and the priests scattered, that man had no way to keep it and was finished.

“Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.” Christ's sacrifice does away with the animal sacrifice, so whoever runs back to animals to atone for sin rejects what Christ did on the cross. Paul is not throwing out the commandments. He is rejecting the sacrifice that was bewitching the Galatians. So “Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.”

precepts.label: Luke 1:68-74
precepts.why:
Leviticus 26 says that even “when they be in the land of their enemies”, like today here in America, “I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly”. Then: “But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors”. Who said bloodline ain’t important? The Bible says he will remember the covenant of your ancestors. Luke 1 is saying the same thing in the New Testament.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. The horn of salvation is Christ. He is the king, out of the house of David. “As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. That is what Leviticus 26 is saying: in the land of their enemies he will not cast them away.

“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers”, our ancestors, “and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham”. That is the covenant of the ancestors in Leviticus 26:45, remembered for their sakes and brought to pass through Christ.

And what is it for? “that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear”. The God who brought our fathers out of Egypt in the sight of the heathen has not broken his covenant with us. He will deliver us out of the hand of our enemies so that we serve him without fear.

precepts.label: John 10:30
precepts.why:
“Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord.” One mind, one body: we start with the order first. The Lord our God is one Lord, and Christ shows what that oneness looks like: “I and my Father are one.”

Is there a division between Christ and his Father? No. They are on one accord. Two persons, the Father and the Son, and yet one, because the Son is in full agreement with the Father.

That is what we as a body have to be: one, in unison, in sync. This is why we have been able to accomplish the amazing things we have in this body, in this congregation: because we are one. Many of our people today have a social religion, more like a superstition, believing what society told them to do. We rely on the scriptures and believe on the Lord as it is written, and the scripture says the Lord is one and Christ is one with him.

precepts.label: John 5:30
precepts.why:
How are Christ and the Father one? Christ does what his Father tells him to do. “I can of mine own self do nothing”: Christ said it himself. “as I hear, I judge”: as I'm told, that's what I do. “and my judgment is just”: the things he does are justified, “because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

He didn't do what he wanted to do; he did what the Father told him to do. You see how that works? He says, I don't do what I want to, I do what the Father tells me to, and yet the scripture says he and his Father are one.

That is the oneness of Deuteronomy 6:4. Being one is not everybody doing their own will; it is every member doing the will of the one who is over him. That is how Christ is one with the Father, and how the body is one with Christ.

precepts.label: John 14:20-21
precepts.why:
Christ warned of his departure, when he would no longer be with them in the body: “At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.” What does it mean? Christ does what his Father tells him to do, Christ comes and tells us what to do, and we keep those commandments.

“He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me.” What commandments? The Father's commandments, all of them. We ain't Christians up in here picking and choosing and cherry picking, hopping and skipping around. Everything the Father told us to do: those are the commandments. The one who has them and keeps them is the man or woman that loves Christ, that loves the Lord.

“and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him.” He is explaining the manifestation, how you receive the Holy Spirit. In order to have the Holy Spirit, you must be one with the Most High God and his Son.

That is how we keep the first commandment, to “love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might”: by keeping his commandments, and being one with the Father and the Son as they are one.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:1
precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 7:6 says the Lord chose Israel “to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.” Deuteronomy 28:1 says it as well, with the condition attached: “if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth.”

If God says we are above all people and above all nations, then why can we not do the things we have a concrete visual example of other nations doing, and doing for decades? When one of the Amish gets married, the community comes together and builds a house for that couple, and there is no mortgage attached to it. They do not even have power cars. We have enough knowledge, enough builders, plumbers and concrete men; we can do this too, at a higher level.

It is going to take work to build this kingdom: work, and faith that we can do the work, shown by our actions. We need to fix our credit scores, fix our health, learn group economics, and work together in the trades, so that when the tough times come, losing your job because of your last name or because you are tracked, we have things set up to help each other.

This is the highway of the upright, the Israelite's strait journey. Ezra saw that “A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things”, but “The entrance thereof is narrow, and is set in a dangerous place to fall”, with fire on the right hand and deep water on the left, and one path “so small that there could but one man go there at once.” That city is the kingdom of heaven, and we must pass through all these things in this captivity to inherit it.

At the end of it, “the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.” We were ransomed out to the nations, but we are returning and gathering together. Being set on high above all nations is the promise to the people who hearken and do the work.

precepts.label: Leviticus 20:26
precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself”. He chose you to be special unto him, set apart from everybody else. So the question is: what makes us holy? What scripture?

Leviticus 20:26 was brought from the floor as the answer: “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.” The Lord is holy, and he severed Israel from other people to be his. That severing is the same set-apart people of Deuteronomy 7:6, chosen “above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

So there has to be something we are doing that makes us different. We cannot be doing the same thing the world is doing, and we cannot be doing what the churches are doing. What severs us from the other people is the laws of God being applied, which is what Romans 7:12 goes on to show.

precepts.label: Romans 7:12
precepts.why:
“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” If the law is holy, and God says you are a holy people, then we are supposed to be a law-abiding people. The laws of God are our constitution, the thing we stand on. That is what makes us holy, what makes us special, what makes us set apart: the laws being applied.

The word of God has no power unless you activate it, and the only way to activate it is to do what it says to do. Other than that it is just pages, just words on a page, just a book. The word is alive and living when you let it live through you by your actions. You become the word, the living example of what it means to be a holy people. That is why the nations say, what a wise and understanding people. They see our actions.

We witness that already at the big events in the big arenas. They say, thousands of black men and nobody smoking weed, no fights breaking out. Then look at what happened in Houston at the rodeo, and how they laughed at us; we are a joke to them. But when we move they ask, how are they so organized, how can they mobilize a few thousand men, put them on the street and file them back in like that, nobody fighting and the place clean? That is the word of God working through us. There is a standard we live by because we are gods on the earth, and it is second nature to us as a nation.

So do not walk in hypocrisy. God gave us something that will make us shine bright and obtain the kingdom. Be that living example to the people.

precepts.label: Matthew 9:36
precepts.why:
“But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.” As Christ went out teaching, healing and doing miracles, he looked and saw that his people fainted. They were out in the streets, they did not worship their God, and their own leaders were taking advantage of them at that time.

It is the same in this captivity as in the time of Rome. Look at our people out there: they are lost, they have no shepherd, they are confused. Not only have the people of the world taken advantage of us, but our own people take advantage too, using the knowledge to get preeminence.

So leaders are motivated because we see the same thing Christ saw: our people afflicted, with no leaders, and looking for a shepherd, which is Christ ultimately. Instead of benefiting ourselves, we see the decayed state of our people and make the sacrifices. To hell with the riches, to hell with the women, having sex, and all those other things. We do whatever it takes to rebuild our nation, so that we can truly benefit from each other and have one shepherd rule over us, with nobody able to take advantage of us.

That is the mind the Lord has put in us, and those who carry it are the ones standing in these last days, speaking with authority and showing our people: this is not the way; let us move according to this holy word and restore this nation. That is what it means to be the holy people God chose.

precepts.label: Sirach 37:19
precepts.why:
“There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” You cannot be a hypocrite, especially in a leadership position. Look at the other camps: they are supposed to be leading the people, but their mind is on the riches, or on how many bodies they can put as a notch in their belt.

There is one that is supposed to be wise. What makes you wise? Keeping the commandments. Those leaders know that. They know they are Israel, they know they are God's chosen people, and they know they are supposed to be keeping the laws. Yet because of their bad intentions and covetousness, because their god is money, or their god is power to move and persuade the people, they are unprofitable to themselves.

And nothing will be hid. Everything that is done will be revealed in time. That is the other side of Deuteronomy 7: the Lord “keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations; And repayeth them that hate him to their face, to destroy them”. If you use a position to lead and teach the people and then take advantage of them, beguiling the sisters into sex, keeping them in a filthy mindset, or taking their money, God will judge you. You hate God and you hate his people.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:68
precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships.” Egypt means bondage, slavery. The children of Israel would go into bondage again, and this time by ships. That is the slave ships: the transatlantic slave trade, the Arab slave trade, the Indian Ocean slave trade, the triangle trade. We were taken on slave ships for 500 years and sold all over the world, and our identity, history, language, culture, diet and clothing were all taken from us. Every people had some form of slavery, but nobody else went through chattel slavery, where there is no end, no going seven years and out. Our whole nation was taken. The Irish did not have their history taken; the Germans did not have their history taken.

“and there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen”: when we got off those slave ships we were sold to our enemies. The slave ships were tight pack and loose pack; the cargo at the bottom was our people. The immigrants came over with clothes on their backs and everything they wanted to bring from their land, established businesses, and are the ones who lend to us today, so they clearly are not the people.

“and no man shall buy you” means nobody is going to redeem you. It cannot mean offering yourself as a slave and nobody buying, because the same verse says you are going to be sold, and we know we were bought. Those who say the so-called white man is the real Jew cannot show the history of him offering himself as a slave with no one buying him. So their understanding is wrong, and those are not the people.

Read on to verse 64: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other.” We went from the west coast of Africa all over the world. “and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” Our fathers never knew a white Jesus, and Jesus never looked like that picture hung in the house and in the church. Wood is symbolic for Christianity, the crucifix; stone for Islam, the cobblestone. Those are the two largest religions the children of Israel have been captured by in these last days, and the Arabs were some of the most brutal slave owners.

This is how Deuteronomy 28:15 is proven. The way you find out who you are is not ancestry.com or 23andMe. You line up the curses and ask: did my forefathers and foremothers go through these things? If they did, you are an Israelite. It is that simple, and nobody else can lay claim to it.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:48
precepts.why:
“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee.” The Bible said we would serve our enemies, “in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things.” We had to go to our oppressors for everything. When we got off those slave ships we were butt naked, and there was no Dollar General in the slave quarters, and no money if there had been.

It is the same thing today. Stop working your job and watch what happens. You want your water turned on, your heat turned on, your car to go: you have to go to your oppressors. An education, a birth certificate, a death certificate, licensing, whatever it is: you have to go to your oppressor. That is “want of all things.”

“and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck”. Show the so-called Jewish man, the Ashkenazi, with a yoke of iron upon his neck. Type Jews with yokes of iron on neck into Google images and you cannot find them. What comes up is black people. Type in Jesus and you know what comes up, and they say Jesus was a Jew; so why aren't white people coming up with yokes of iron on them?

That is identifying us through the scriptures, not through DNA. The curses of Deuteronomy 28:15 came upon us and overtook us, and the yoke of iron is written on our people alone. Bringing that out is called racial idolatry now, but it is just showing people the truth.

“Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed”. I don't care what country you are in, what state, what continent: these curses are following us. That's why we're getting shot down in the streets and killed left and right; the Most High has to do something to wake us back up. We are a destroyed nation, and we haven't understood that yet.

“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder”. The curses are the sign. That is how we know we are the Israelites: the Bible gives us the signs to look out for, in Deuteronomy 28:15-68 and in Genesis 49, and if our spirit resonates with those signs, we are going to realize that we are the Israelites.

That is Romans 8:16: “The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God”. That we, the Israelites, are the children of God. Not the whole world. The spirit itself, the Bible, bears witness with our spirit that we are those children.

And “for a wonder”: we are supposed to be wondering what happened. We are the greatest people on earth; how did we get so low? It will be upon our seed for ever, upon our children until Christ's return. Brothers want to argue the trinity while our people are being killed, holding the name Israel and refusing everything that goes with it. The sign is on us, and the spirit bears witness with ours: we are Israel, and we have to come back to the Lord.

precepts.label: Joshua 2:15-16
precepts.why:
When the king of Jericho sent for the men, Rahab hid them “with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof”, and sent the pursuers the wrong way. Then she went further: “Then she let them down by a cord through the window: for her house was upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall.” “And she said unto them, Get you to the mountain, lest the pursuers meet you; and hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers be returned: and afterward may ye go your way.”

She not only helped the prophets, she helped them with an exit. She gave them a way out and a plan: where to go, how long to hide, and when it would be safe to go their way.

These examples are in here for our learning. In these last days some brothers and sisters are going to be looked to to hide the prophets. As we build this spiritual underground railroad, some of y'all will be required to help one another, and sometimes when you help brothers and sisters you are going to put yourself in danger.

Is that you, sister? Is that you, brother? Are you ready to do that for your nation? Or are you going to sell out to keep this body that gets a headache, gets diarrhea, gets belly aches, coughing and all kind of infirmities? The scriptures tell you we have to be ready in these last days.

That is why Hebrews 13 follows it: “Let brotherly love continue.” “Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.” Start small, in your household. Make that guest room ready to receive a guest; if you can't afford an extra room, instead of buying that leather couch, get a pullout couch. If a prophet is on the run and you can provide shelter for two days, a meal and shelter for a prophet, that is a blessing for you. That is the mindset of Rahab, and the mindset we have to have in these last days.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:17
precepts.why:
Solomon’s mind was on the people. He did not ask for four hundred women or chariots, or to be a king of 4,000; he asked for “an understanding heart to judge thy people”, “for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?” Because he had a mind for the people, the Lord elevated him and gave him more than he even desired for himself. Likewise with us: when we have a mind for the people, the Lord will bless that thing beyond measure.

Sirach says it plainly: “Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” In this truth we are not doing this for ourselves. Captains left at four in the morning, driving, so they could be here to help teach the class. A captain drove down and got here at five in the morning to check the congregation, to check on the saints of the Most High. The bishops travel all over the world; the deacons travel. This is not for ourselves; this is for the nation of Israel, because we understand the kingdom that is at hand.

“but for all them”: this is a nation. You must be nation-minded. A lot of times we are not like that: me, me, me, me, me, and that is all you are concerned with. But all through the Bible the greatest leaders were focused on the nation of Israel and how to move the nation further ahead.

That is the mindset of a leader and the action of a king: like Solomon, labour not for yourself only, but for all the people, and the Lord gives more than you asked.

precepts.label: Tobit 4:12-13
precepts.why:
“But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh”. When you turn against the Lord in this, you turn against your neighbor too, because you are taking foreign women. We know it will turn your heart away from following the Lord, but what does it do to your brother? It says you hate your brother. Tobit shows it.

“Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”. He calls interracial marriage whoredom. “for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.”

“Now therefore, my son, love thy brethren, and despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them”. Don’t despise your brethren. Passing over the daughters of your own people for strange women is despising your brethren in your heart. “for in pride is destruction and much trouble, and in lewdness is decay and great want: for lewdness is the mother of famine.”

That is exactly where Solomon went. The Lord had said of those nations, “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods”, and Solomon clave unto them in love. His wives turned away his heart after Ashtoreth, Milcom, Chemosh and Molech, and he built high places for them and for all his strange wives. That is how syncretism enters: through the strange wife, and it begins by despising your own people.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 35:1
precepts.why:
Solomon offered “according to the commandment of Moses”, on the sabbaths, the new moons and the solemn feasts, “three times in the year”: the feast of unleavened bread, the feast of weeks and the feast of tabernacles. It is the same law given in Deuteronomy 16:16: “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God”, and “they shall not appear before the Lord empty.” So we are supposed to gather and give an offering three times a year. We come together.

But do we give a physical offering today? No. So what do we offer? We offer ourselves; we offer obedience. Sirach puts it plainly: “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.”

Keeping the law is the offering. The one who takes heed to the commandment is not coming before the Lord empty; his obedience is his peace offering. That is how Israel keeps these feasts now, the feast of weeks, which is Pentecost, among them: by gathering together and bringing a life that keeps the commandments.

thread.text: So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 11:16
precepts.why:
“So built we the wall”: all through our history, the forefathers were building. What we are doing today is nothing different from what they always did, and Ezekiel shows the kind of building the Lord gives us while we are scattered.

“Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.” Israel was cast far off and scattered, and the Lord still gave them little sanctuaries in the lands where they came.

When Paul went to Galatia, to Colossae, to Corinth and to Thessalonica, those were sanctuaries, just like the ones you see today. The schools are those little sanctuaries in the countries, and each and every one of us put a hand into building each and every one of them.

So the wall of Nehemiah and the little sanctuary of Ezekiel are the same work. The people built because they had a mind to work, and that mind to work is what leadership has to put into the people now.

precepts.label: Matthew 6:22
precepts.why:
The people built the wall because they “had a mind to work.” This is how a leader’s mindset must be, and Christ shows it: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”

A single eye is being locked in, what they call laser focus. Whatever you are locked in on, that is what you are going to see. That is all you are going to see, and that is all that matters.

And when the leader is like that, guess who else is going to be like that? Everybody underneath him. The single eye of the one at the head fills the whole body with light, so the whole camp takes on his focus.

That is why the wall got built. The mind to work in the people starts with the mind of the one leading them.

precepts.label: Sirach 10:1-2
precepts.why:
“A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered. As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” However the leader is, that is how the men under him are going to be.

So when you see these other camps that look disorganized, that are talking about rape, that have not built anything in years, find their leaders, and that is what you will see. When you see us traveling all over the world, building institutions, organizations within the organization, look at our leaders. We are the representation of our leadership.

When we go to Chicago we are not on film eating chicken and pizza in the hood at midnight. How is that a leader of a congregation? You will never see a bishop or a deacon put out a video like that. When we went to Chicago, we went to O’Block teaching the word of the Lord.

Everything rises and falls on leadership. There are cities where the leader was changed and the camp took off, and other places where the leader left and everything fell apart. You are who your leader is. That is why everybody wants to ask the Bishop for the secret sauce, but what they do not understand is that Christ is at the head and we are all following Christ. The Most High is building 144,000 leaders, sealed with the law of God, and nothing they try can stop it.

That is why the people of Nehemiah had a mind to work: the wall reflects the ones leading the building.

precepts.label: Isaiah 6:8
precepts.why:
Job 33:23 speaks of “a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand”. You are the interpreter, brother, and you are that one among a thousand. When you are one among a thousand, that makes you a leader, and you have to have the mind of a leader. Any place you step into, your mindset shouldn't be to fit in; you should be figuring out how to make it better. Joseph didn't go into Egypt and just sit there; he asked how we are going to solve the problem. The Lord gave us wisdom, discretion, judgment and skill sets.

The first thing in the mindset of a leader is that he believes he can get the job done. That is what separates you from everybody else. When an issue arises, you don't run. You raise your hand, you volunteer, you figure out a solution to the problem.

Isaiah shows it: “Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Who is going to go on our behalf? “Then said I, Here am I; send me.” That's the mindset of a leader.

That is the same thing David did. Everybody kept crying about the situation, and David said, where is Goliath at? Show me. The first thing you have to have is a willingness and a belief in completing the task, whatever it may be, and that mindset alone sets you apart. That is what the Lord has put in your spirit to do: not an unsure mind that says maybe I can, but send me.

precepts.label: Job 36:15
precepts.why:
Job 36:10 says the Lord “openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity”: he commanded, requested and called you to return from iniquity back to your heritage. Verse 15 shows where he opens those ears: “He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.”

The poor here are our people. It was through the oppression of the oppressor, and through the religion he gave us, that our ears were opened. Esau is not poor. They are rich through robbery, and that continues to this day. We are a people robbed and spoiled and hid in prison houses, as Isaiah 42 says, and it is being played out in real time.

Just because you are not in the prison system doesn't mean you are not in captivity. Deuteronomy 28:15-68 applies to us: the Lord gave us the warning, we didn't take heed, and the curses are in full effect. The 13th Amendment was supposed to end slavery, but its clause, except as punishment for crime, made the loophole that fills the prisons with our people for free labor. Slavery was never abolished; it evolved. They framed mischief and made it law, like the throne of iniquity that “frameth mischief by a law.” A warden speaks of a young man's sweat equity instead of the death penalty, the same spirit as the Willie Lynch letter: don't kill him, it's not good economics.

This is still the land of our captivity, and the enemy got crafty with us. But in that oppression the Lord opened our ears. We were deaf and now we hear discipline; we were blind and now we see. We are not supposed to be at rest in this land. Your 9-to-5 is not your purpose; your purpose is to keep his commandments, remember that you are called and requested of God, and magnify his law upon the earth.

precepts.label: Hosea 5:15
precepts.why:
“He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.” When our people are oppressed, God opens their ears. All the things Trump is doing, and ICE is doing in the streets and in the black community, are God opening your ears. For the last 60 years our people have been lost and confused, following the American dream and thinking America is about equal rights and opportunity. God said, no, this place is not your rest. So he turns up the oppression, because that is the only time we as a people turn to God: when bad things start happening to us.

Hosea says it: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” Until we acknowledge our offence and seek God's face.

In our affliction we will seek him early: before it is too late, before we die, before judgment comes. So God is allowing Trump to do these things in the black community with these ICE agents so that you will seek him. Our people are realizing that the American dream is exactly what it is, a dream, and that there is no such thing here as justice and equal rights. That is why judgment starts first with the house of God.

precepts.label: Psalms 78:33
precepts.why:
Psalm 78 shows the same pattern: “Therefore their days did he consume in vanity, and their years in trouble.” The trouble is affliction. “When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned and enquired early after God.”

When God slew us. What do you see taking place all over the streets right now? Our people being oppressed, locked up, put in prison by ICE officers. Then we seek God. That is when we return and enquire early after the Lord: when bad things start happening to us.

That is why judgment must begin first at the house of the Lord. Number one, for us to turn back to our God. Number two, to prove us: as you turn to him, bad things will happen to see whether you believe and trust in him. “And they remembered that God was their rock, and the high God their redeemer.” He is the one who will redeem us from the condition we are in.

And Isaiah 30 gives the teachers their job: though the Lord gives the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, the teachers will not be removed into a corner any more. As our people cry under the affliction, we go to them and tell them why it is happening: this is the way, walk ye in it. Not guns, as some are calling for; the word of God is what will change our people and bring destruction on this place.

thread.text: I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother’s belly.

classes.title: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.label: Jeremiah 32:27
precepts.why:
“I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother’s belly.” The trinitarians read it this way: when Christ came into the world as a human being, that's when his Father became his God. The Father has divine essence, the Holy Spirit has divine essence, the Son has divine essence, so when Christ came on the earth keeping humanity and godhood, he is his own god. And not only that: he is his own god and he has a God above him. That's two. It's a ridiculous argument.

“Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?” The Father is the God of all flesh. So if Christ is the essence of his Father, then Christ becomes the God of his own humanity, God over his own flesh. It's madness. Pressed with it in the debate, the trinitarian answered exactly that: Christ is God over his own flesh. And his own side laughed at him; you could see his friend's face in the back. They know that's stupid.

That one question stumped them. There is no scripture that says the heavenly Father becomes his God when he is human, as opposed to being his God always. That's pure theology. Ask them where the Bible says it. Nowhere in Psalms 22 do we read that Christ, out of his mother's womb, is fully God and fully man. That is a Greco-Roman hermeneutical interpretation; they even admitted there is an element of philosophy in it. It isn't an element; it's full-blown philosophy.

The scripture is clear. Resurrected and glorified, Christ says “my God” four times in one verse: “Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God.” And risen from the dead, “I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.” Even “being in the form of God”, he “thought it not robbery to be equal with God”, but “made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant”: God or man, he knew the Father was above him. These men follow the Greeks, “Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all”. They are unreasonable people, going in circles like a cartwheel, and you cannot waste your time with them.

classes.title: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:42
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezra, “I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” God's judgment goes round like a ring, a wheel. It comes around without fail, the last no slower than the first.

The scriptures say God shall be known in his judgments. So when Deuteronomy says that when we sin we will find ourselves back in captivity, in slavery and in prison houses, and we look around and see those conditions, his judgment stands. It is sure, and his prophecies are fulfilled. That is how we show that God is here: so take heed and fear God.

That is the frame for Psalms 94:20: “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” The 13th Amendment abolished slavery except as punishment for crime. Within fifteen years the Southern states were imprisoning black Americans at ten times the rate of whites; they made loitering and vagrancy felonies and leased the convicts out for forced labor. Today prison labor makes billions while inmates earn cents an hour. They framed mischief by a law and misled us with democracy and freedom. Slavery did not end; it evolved.

A former warden testified that a young defendant should get life without parole instead of death because the prison could use him: he is young, he is healthy, we need that sweat equity. That is the Willie Lynch letter: beat him within an inch of his life but don't kill him, because it is not good for economics.

The throne of iniquity has no fellowship with Christ: not their holidays, not their man-made religions, and no, the president is not God. Some people do need to be locked up if they rob and steal. But the judgment keeps turning like a ring, and what we institute is keeping God's commandments, so that you stay far from all of that.

thread.label: Psalms 96:5
thread.text: For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.

classes.title: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:47
precepts.why:
“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. The Lord gave us the abundance of all things, and we did not want to serve him for it. So he caused us to serve our enemies, and that is why we ended up falling underneath these people. That is not where our position is supposed to be.

Before we went into captivity we were celebrating the gods of the nations, and the Lord had a problem with that. Psalms 96:5 is his message and warning to us: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.” Our God made everything; that is the God we are connected with. So-called Christmas, Thanksgiving and so-called New Year's are pagan, evil hella days, not holy days. How can you talk about Thanksgiving on stolen land?

We are not the nations. “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” “He hath not dealt so with any nation”. Our customs are his statutes and judgments; we have the Bible, not idols. And Jeremiah 10 says, “Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel”, “Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them.” Astrology, witchcraft and voodoo are the nations' problem, not ours. The Israelites are a special people, set above the nations, the jewels of God, and you have to see yourselves that way.

“For the customs of the people are vain”, void of anything credible: “one cutteth a tree out of the forest”, and “They deck it with silver and with gold”. That was the custom in the Babylonian empire, four empires before Christ was born in the time of Rome. What do lights, tin and silver on a tree have to do with Christ? Nothing. It is Sol Invictus, the unconquered sun, sun worship commemorating Nimrod, Tammuz, whom the women wept for in Ezekiel 8, celebrated on December 25th. Our people know Christ has nothing to do with it, the same way the Bible gives no white Jesus, but they will not stand up for truth.

Serving the gods of the nations instead of serving the Lord with gladness is what put us under our enemies. Anybody who continues to celebrate that madness now knows better and will be judged by the Most High.

thread.label: Psalms 101:5
thread.text: Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off: him that hath an high look and a proud heart will not I suffer.

classes.title: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.label: Proverbs 10:18
precepts.why:
“Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off”: God will cut you off, cut off from the book of the living. Proverbs shows what is really behind slander: “He that hideth hatred with lying lips, and he that uttereth a slander, is a fool.”

When somebody lies on you or slanders you, what that really says is that there is hatred there. The lying lips are hiding hatred.

“and he that uttereth a slander”: you had Tyre Gas, you had Lightfoot, you had these guys uttering slanders, and their followers talk that way because their leaders are the same way. They run with slander. As a leader you are supposed to hear an outrageous lie and say, I do not believe that. One woman said we came to Canada on a magic school bus, and some leaders believed it.

God says you are a fool to listen to lies, run with them and put them out there. Slander is defamation: running with an accusation without two or three witnesses, and God cuts that man off.

precepts.label: Proverbs 26:28
precepts.why:
“A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.” If you lie on somebody and run with slander, it says that you hate the one who is afflicted by it.

You heard it plainly from one of them: I am here to down IUIC. That is the hatred behind the lying tongue that Psalms 101 says God will cut off.

Every matter is to be established by two or three witnesses. What was put out about Captain Obadiah was one witness, and that witness was a lie. The charges were dropped; the footage and the witnesses showed he was defending himself. It is sad that the white man had to come and say he was defending himself, when those who talk about righteous judgment could not understand something that simple. In London, when our sister died, people said IUIC killed her and hid evidence, and the investigators showed that the man who did it was evil and we had nothing to do with it.

A false witness is called slander, or defamation, and false witness can get you killed. By the law, what was to be done to the brother you slandered is to be done unto you. We do not have power to institute that, but Esau’s court system has defamation, and that is how it is going to be done now: whatever you put out against the truth, you had better be able to prove it, or you will have to come up out of the pockets. That is to protect the ministry of Christ, because the lies are put out to blame the ministry.

precepts.label: Sirach 11:9
precepts.why:
“Strive not in a matter that concerneth thee not; and sit not in judgment with sinners.” That is why so many brothers get caught up in suits: striving in things that do not concern them, things they know nothing about. You just hear something and you are running your mouth.

To sit in judgment with sinners is sitting in counsel with brothers that are not right, brothers who were put out of the school, like Judah Mack and Titus.

Read on: “My son, meddle not with many matters: for if thou meddle much, thou shalt not be innocent.” This is for those who keep running their mouths talking about us. You meddle in matters that do not concern you, and you are not going to be innocent. That is why legal measures are being taken: to teach men to control their mouths, and to make sure that when you say something, it is true.

So the privy slanderer of Psalms 101 is the man who strives in what does not concern him and sits with sinners, and God will cut him off.

precepts.label: Matthew 4:17
precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”. You cannot have a good understanding if you are not keeping the commandments. It is biblically impossible to understand this Bible while you are not observing the laws of God. There is no way around it. All the foolishness that gets exposed comes from those that refuse to repent and keep God's commandments.

That is why Christ's message from the start was this: “From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.”

So many of our brothers and sisters out in the world have yet to come to grips with what we are here for. Being an Israelite in Christ is not about dressing up as an Israelite. It's not about arguing with white folks in the streets. It's not about flexing your muscles and trying to be a tough guy. And no, it is not about multiple wives.

Being an Israelite in Christ is about observing the Most High God's commandments and faith in his Son, so that we don't die when the Lord returns. The kingdom of heaven is at hand, and you are at risk if you do not repent and seek the kingdom. Point blank, period.

Those who deny Christ and deny keeping the commandments, because they want to fulfil their own lust, come up with absurd breakdowns of scripture. Without repentance there is no good understanding.

thread.label: Psalms 119:18
thread.text: Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.

classes.title: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.label: Matthew 5:48
precepts.why:
Christ says it plainly: “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” You see it right there in red. For those taking notes, those new to this, those still on the fence: this is Christ himself speaking.

That is the wondrous thing the psalmist asks to behold: “Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” When I keep God’s commandments, the wondrous thing I see out of them is that he wants me to be like him. God gave law so that we can be like unto him, perfect as our Father in heaven is perfect.

Those eyes are not only the bodily eyes. They are the spiritual eyes, the insight to see this word and the situation we are in, and to understand that it is all spiritual. That is why we have to delve into the scriptures and meditate, so that we can behold the wondrous things out of God’s law, and after we understand and observe, apply it and be like our Father.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:2
precepts.why:
This is what Christ’s words meant in the Old Testament. The Lord told Moses: “Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the Lord your God am holy.” God is holy, and he says, you shall be holy.

Holiness is us coming into perfection. That is the wondrous thing out of God’s law in Psalms 119:18: the law is given so that his children can become like him.

What makes us perfect? Read on in Psalms 19. “The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.” The sun, the moon and the stars prove there must be a God; but how much more should you show him in your conversation and your actions, by not sinning? Then: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul”. The law is perfect because God’s laws are his ways, his habits, and he gave them unto his children. It converts us from darkness into light, from the power of Satan unto the power of God, for the redemption of our souls.

Then: “the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were simple, lost through slavery and oppression, calling ourselves anything but who we are. Coming back to understanding that we are the Israelites, and striving for perfection by keeping the law, is our souls being converted. And you cannot come to perfection without trials: gold is tried in the fire.

thread.text: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!

classes.title: Member's In The Body

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 32:30
precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Why is that good and pleasant? It's the only way we grow, keeping the commandments together as a unit; without unity there is disorder, and nothing gets built. But the reason it is so important is that we can't be stopped when we are unified. Moses shows it: “How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight”?

Unity. That's how we are going to do it: through us together, unified in Christ. Hence the name Israel United in Christ. We can move mountains. It's that type of unity we have to come to and understand, because without it, brothers, we won't do nothing.

Look at some of the others, not doing anything. They don't aspire to do anything; they're fine just where they're at, cool just being in the house, and they will keep doing videos from their garages. But we have worldwide goals. The vision here has been set at a worldwide standard. If you don't have worldwide aspirations, you're not going to do worldwide things. If you think small, you'll stay small. Shoot for the stars.

The sixty-man camp of 2013 showed it: that small number organized and unified set a standard in the nation, and today one phone call could bring a thousand men. That is one chasing a thousand and two putting ten thousand to flight, when brethren dwell together in unity.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:16
precepts.why:
Wisdom says, “Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold.” What are those riches? Colossians shows it: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.”

The riches we are looking for are not money, though people think they are. We need the durable riches, which is wisdom: the word of Christ dwelling in us richly. And this is what we are supposed to do with it: teach and admonish one another.

God says, I am giving it to you. But you are walking in hypocrisy, distracted by covetousness, and a man’s life does not consist of the abundance of what he has. That was not their kingdom at that point, and all of this is coming to an end anyway. God has something far better than what you are looking at, and you are about to throw it away for this world.

Now you understand what the scripture is saying, so you have no excuse. Much is given, so much is required, and the one who knew will be beaten with many stripes. So I have to walk in that, stand in that space and be that, or get ready to get beat. The durable riches of Proverbs 8 are the word living in us richly, and they have to be walked in.

thread.text: If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest.

classes.title: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.label: Sirach 33:5
precepts.why:
“If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man”: if a wise man debates with a stupid man or woman. And “whether he rage or laugh”: whether that fool laughs at it or is angry at it, “there is no rest.” There is no conclusion. It is a circular argument; you argue the same thing over and over again and it goes nowhere.

Sirach shows why: “The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.” The fool is a circular idiot. His mind just goes in circles, nonstop. That is the Trinity man: three is one, one is three, they are all the same, the Father and the Son of one substance. Round and round, and you cannot win. They are dead set in it, their minds sealed as with a hot iron.

Show them that the Father has sons, the children of Israel, and they cannot understand it: no, they are all one. Stump them in a debate and they keep going: but what about this? It is ongoing. It is a cartwheel. They will not yield to reason. Even the German had some sense when he called insanity doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.

So leave that negro alone. You are wasting your time. These are unreasonable people, and you have to let them go. The wise man who keeps contending with the fool gets no rest, because the fool's heart only rolls in circles of nonsense.
