precepts.label: Romans 8:19
precepts.why:
“Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” Man was put on this earth to rule it with God's commandments, and because we are not doing that, the earth is suffering; we are not in power. The earth was made to receive your direction, men.

Paul shows it: “For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” Expectation means I am expecting something, and earnestly means with a begging type of attitude. The creation is earnestly waiting for the manifestation, and manifestation means the growth: time for us to stop being kids and manifest into men, to get ourselves together. The earth is waiting for the sons of God to manifest into gods, that is, to rule this planet properly.

And righteous women are waiting for that too. The woman is called woman because she is of man, and she is like the earth: you plant your seed in her and she brings forth fruit, but she needs your guidance. She is supposed to revolve around you, and when you are not in rulership she is out of orbit, like a satellite floating in space with no direction. That is why women cry, where are our black men? The father figure in the house got destroyed.

All of it fell apart when we broke the laws of the Most High from the very beginning, when the woman was out of order with her husband. So it is up to us men to fulfil the duty of manhood to fix it: to marry, build a nation, and rule rightly. That is what the whole creation is waiting on.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:14
precepts.why:
Verse 13 gives the whole duty of man; verse 14 gives the reason: “For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” For means because. Keep his commandments, because this is the whole reason God put man on the earth, and because God shall bring every work into judgment.

So if we are not dealing with our marriages properly, there is going to be a judgment for that, and we are looking at it. People try to figure out the problem in the black community: the marriages are messed up. Whoring, adultery, fornication. A little leaven will destroy the whole congregation, and it has to be rooted out like a cancer.

“with every secret thing”: the nasty stuff people do behind closed doors, thinking nobody sees. In nearly 35 years in this truth, we have seen the Most High bring out what people thought they could hide, and he brings it out at the worst time for you. Like applying for a job years later, thinking you got away with it, and they pull records you didn't know existed: get out of my office. That's how the Lord is.

So keep your slate clean. Be a disciplined man: you may not always be motivated, but you must always be disciplined. When sin comes before you, it stops right there. Because every work, good or evil, is going to come out, we have to be men of holiness, integrity, righteousness, dignity, honor and valor. That is the whole duty of man.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 10:20
precepts.why:
God shall bring every secret thing into judgment, and the Lord even calls a bird to bring it out: “Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.” We have sat in judgments where they asked, how did he find out? It's that damn bird. Somebody might think it's a literal bird flying around; I took every precaution. But the Most High is going to bring it out anyway. That's why it says every secret thing.

No, not in thy thought. Some people speak against the council and the leadership, or have evil thoughts against the leaders, and think they will get away with it. The Most High put leadership to watch over you, and that is not an easy job. Leaders must give an account, good or bad. The goal is to give a good account: the brother came in one way and now he is a man of valor, married, moving in the right direction; the sister listened to counsel and got herself together. When they will not take counsel, the leader still has to give an account, with grief.

This is how we should have grown up. We grew up in a lawless society; in slavery the fathers were stripped from the homes and the men forced to give their seed but not allowed to raise it. The matter will be told on you in your evil, so fear God, keep his commandments, and honor the ones set over you.

thread.label: Isaiah 1:3
thread.text: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.

classes.title: 2025 Recap: Different Times, Same Truth

precepts.label: Ezekiel 3:6
precepts.why:
“The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.” The Israelites are the only people on the face of the earth who do not know who they are. Ask around and you get a million answers: black, colored, African-American, Nuwabian, the Asiatic black man, Muslim, Christian, we are all one in Christ. Ask a white man and he is Polish; others can trace their lineage back to the village their ancestors came from.

“my people doth not consider”: not only do we not know who we are, we do not even consider that we could be the people of this book. We have been teaching it for forty years, and now there are urban apologists whose whole life is set around proving us wrong. We are the only people who will fight not to be God’s chosen. On a show like The Bachelor all the nations would run to be the bride of Christ, with the promises and the covenant; black people are the only ones saying, Don’t nobody want him.

Ezekiel shows it: “Not to many people of a strange speech and of an hard language, whose words thou canst not understand. Surely, had I sent thee to them, they would have hearkened unto thee.” God did not send the prophet to a people of a hard language. If he had, they would have hearkened in a heartbeat.

That is how we know we are the people. We have the best videos, the best music, the best teachers; the Bishops and Deacons broke the book down precept upon precept from the first book to Revelation, as no pastor in the history of Christianity ever touched, and still the negro says, Nah, I’m good, what about John 3:16? The other nations would hearken. Israel doth not know and doth not consider.

thread.label: Isaiah 1:4-5
thread.text: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears
Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:24
precepts.why:
Isaiah cries, “Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity”. We are laden: like a ladle dipped in soup, we are soaked and drenched with iniquity. A sinful nation means we break God's laws. So what is sin? Ezra answers: “Woe to them that sin, and keep not my commandments! saith the Lord.”

Sin is when we don't keep God's commandments. Brothers, put this in your arsenal. We always go to 1 John 5:3, of course, but we have to understand that it is precept upon precept, and Ezra says the same thing.

And who are the people that were given God's commandments? The twelve tribes of Israel. That is who Isaiah is calling the sinful nation. He was never talking about the Hittites or anybody but the Israelites.

This matters now because wars are here, and it is no time to think you are ready. You may wear your fringes, keep your beard right, keep the Sabbath and put the pork down, but still battle with patience, anger, a brawling spirit, an evil eye, or the weed you won't put down. Woe to them that sin. The whole head is sick: you're sick and I'm sick, and we have to keep getting right.

precepts.label: Psalms 147:19-20
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the sinful nation has “provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger”. To prove which nation that is: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” Jacob was the forefather of the twelve tribes, and his name later became Israel. The statutes and the judgments were given to the nation of Israel.

“He hath not dealt so with any nation”. So for modern-day Christians to say that God is dealing with all nations and all people, they don't know the Bible.

Then: “and as for his judgments, they have not known them.” The Israelites are the ones that get judged. That is why Black people went into slavery, in the trans-Saharan slave trade and the trans-Atlantic slave trade, and many other times in history we have served our enemies in slavery.

So Isaiah was never talking about anybody but the Israelites. We are the seed of evildoers who call evil good and good evil, led astray by Christian pastors and the leaders in the mosques. From 1865 to 1965 we lived under more overt racism, but we had civility, women had a dress code, and there was an order to talk to a sister. Since 1965 we have gained almost twenty million abortions by Black women alone and the dumbest generation of children with the smartest technology. We provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, and that is why we went into slavery.

thread.label: Isaiah 9:6-7
thread.text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.label: John 14:8-9
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls the son that is given “The everlasting Father.” Most Christians, and even some Israelites, cannot explain that, because they have not figured out that the everlasting Father in the Old Testament was Christ. They say we always spoke to the Father. No, you did not speak to the Father; you spoke to Christ. That is why he is called the everlasting Father. John 14 is a precept for it.

“Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.” See Christ’s response: “Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?”

Yes, Christ looks like his Father. But what is he actually telling Philip? I created you. I am your Father, your everlasting Father. You were brought forth through me.

Remember, Christ is the only begotten of the Father. That means the Father created only Christ, and then told Christ to create everything else. So when Isaiah names the child born unto us “The mighty God, The everlasting Father”, it is because everything that exists was brought forth through him. That is why Philip, who had been with him so long, should have known him.

precepts.label: John 1:1-3
precepts.why:
In case anyone is still confused about why Christ is called “The everlasting Father”, John 1 settles it. We have to shake the Christian thoughts.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Christ was in the beginning with God, and he was God. “The same was in the beginning with God.” God is a plural there.

Then the part that matters: “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by Christ, and without Christ was not any thing made that was made. The Father only begat Christ, and through Christ everything else was created.

That is why he said to Philip, “Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip?” I created all of this. That is too heavy for a Negro, because you have Baptist on your mind and Catholic in your head. It was hard for us in the beginning too, but the Most High has shown us. Let it marinate.

So the child born and the son given in Isaiah 9:6, with the government upon his shoulder, is the same one who made all things: the Word, the mighty God, the everlasting Father.

precepts.label: Matthew 13:31-32
precepts.why:
“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Christ explains that increase in Matthew 13: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.” If you grew up in the city you may not know what a mustard seed looks like; it is one of the smallest of all seeds.

“but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs.” When it is grown: that is the increase of his government. It starts small. What we have here is small. We may think we have a lot, but this is nothing yet; we are still at the mustard seed stage.

And the kingdom of heaven is a government, not a church group. That is why it behooves us to learn God’s laws, commandments and statutes: to set up a government you need everything that makes a community, and God’s laws are going to filter everything for us. Right now we think small. God says think bigger. A house? Bigger. Property? Bigger. The world is ours, and for the world to be ours we have to be able to set all of that up.

Think how the Most High uses something as small as the human mind. As a man thinketh, so is he. Everything you lay your eyes on, every object and invention, was a thought first. We shortchange ourselves with doubt, but that is not what God made. Untapped greatness is waiting to bud; remove the doubt and the fear and let the Lord work on that head.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:12-21
precepts.why:
The mustard seed government is small now, and we think small. Compare what God did for Solomon with where we are today.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” Solomon learned wisdom and gave it out freely, and that is what we are doing today: we don’t hide the riches of the wisdom of God. “For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning.” If we use this wisdom we become the friends of God. And it comes from learning, not once but daily; that is what the classes every day are about.

“For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements.” You might say you know how the world was made. You don’t: what elements make the air, what elements were made for the sun? Solomon understood that. He knew “The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”, from Adam to the second coming of Christ. He knew “the alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons”, “The circuits of years, and the positions of stars.”

“The natures of living creatures”: Esau puts cameras on animals, even in their butts, to learn how they defecate, trying to get on Solomon’s level with all that freakiness. Solomon knew “the furies of wild beasts”, “the violence of winds”, the tornadoes and storms, “the reasonings of men”, “the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots”, which herb is for what, and “all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.”

We are not even on Solomon’s level yet. We need the Lord to open our minds up to get there, and when he does we will be on that level and greater. That is what the mustard seed is about: we start small and it grows. This is the beginning of that government.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 23:5-6
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the government shall be upon his shoulder, “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice.” Jeremiah says the same: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch.” That righteous Branch is Christ.

“and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” See what he is going to do: execute judgment and justice in the earth. The nations don’t want that. Some of us in here may not want that either: I don’t want no justice and judgment, hell no. Yes, it is coming anyway.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.”

So the throne of David in Isaiah 9 is the reign of this King, the Branch raised unto David. The increase of his government is a kingdom of judgment and justice, of law and order, and in his days Judah is saved and Israel dwells safely. That is why we learn God’s laws now: it is the government we are going to live under.

thread.label: Isaiah 14:4,16-17
thread.text: That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!

classes.title: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.label: Revelation 17:5
precepts.why:
Isaiah says “thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon.” We know from Psalms 137 that the United States of America is the daughter of Babylon, and Isaiah is speaking prophetically of Babylon the Great to come, the same one John wrote about in Revelation.

“And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS.” Is that saying Babylon is one big brothel, with the main hoe in the United States pimping out the other hoes? No. It is similitude.

Think about who wrote it. John lived way after Isaiah, during the Roman Empire, long after ancient Babylon had fallen. Why would John be writing about ancient Babylon? He is talking about the same Babylon the Great Isaiah saw: the United States of America. This is not talking about Iraq.

Everybody sees it except the Israelites. They will say no one knows who this is. Are you kidding me? Our Black people, our Hispanics and Native Americans who cannot see it, we hope the Lord opens your eyes.

That is why Isaiah asks, “Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms; That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof?” The man is the so-called white man running the United States, whose real power began with the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in '45. He is weakening the nations, even his own allies like India and Japan, which depend on oil coming through the Strait of Hormuz, and God is hardening the hearts of Trump's circle to do just what he wants, as he did with Egypt.

thread.text: Whom the Lord of hosts shall bless, saying, Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance.

precepts.label: Isaiah 27:12-13
precepts.why:
“Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance.” That is the one verse they might run with: see, Egypt is his people and Assyria is his people, so the Egyptians and the Assyrians are saved too. No problem. Go over a few chapters and see where this Egypt and Assyria are.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel.” Gathered one by one: who? The children of Israel.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the great trumpet shall be blown”: that is Christ coming. “And they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt.” Earlier it said Egypt and Assyria; here it is the land of Assyria and the land of Egypt, and the ones coming out of them are the children of Israel. So who is “Egypt my people” and Assyria? Israelites.

“And shall worship the Lord in the holy mount at Jerusalem.” My people in Egypt and my people in Assyria means Israel in those lands, scattered there and gathered out one by one to worship at Jerusalem. That is how precepts work: you don't build a doctrine for another nation on one verse.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:11
precepts.why:
Just in case Isaiah 27 is not enough, beat a dead horse. “And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people.” That is the same gathering we read in Isaiah 27.

From where? “Which shall be left, from Assyria”: my people. “And from Egypt”: Egypt, my people. “And from Pathros”: still Egypt, my people. “And from Cush, and from Elam”: Elam is Iran and Pakistan, my people. “And from Shinar”: Shinar is Iraq, my people. “And from Hamath”: Syria, my people. “And from the islands of the sea”: the islands, whether the Mediterranean or the Caribbean. That is his people.

It names Assyria and Egypt right there with the rest, and in every one of those places it is the remnant of his people that he recovers, not the nations of those lands. So when Isaiah 19 says “Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands”, it is speaking of Israel scattered in Egypt and Assyria, whom the Lord recovers the second time.

precepts.label: Zechariah 10:6-10
precepts.why:
One more, just in case. “And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them again to place them.” Bring them again: that is the second time, the recovering of Isaiah 11. “For I have mercy upon them: and they shall be as though I had not cast them off”: as though they had never been in captivity. “For I am the Lord their God, and will hear them.”

“And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man, and their heart shall rejoice as through wine: yea, their children shall see it, and be glad.” “I will hiss for them, and gather them; for I have redeemed them.” Both Judah and Joseph, Judah and Ephraim: he will gather all twelve tribes. “And they shall increase as they have increased. And I will sow them among the people: and they shall remember me in far countries; and they shall live with their children, and turn again.”

“I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria.” Bring who again? All twelve tribes, out of Egypt and out of Assyria, the same as Isaiah 11:11. “And I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them.”

So what does “Egypt my people” and “Assyria the work of my hands” mean? It means Israel in those lands. That makes four scriptures, and there is no arguing with it. That is called precepts.

precepts.label: Matthew 15:7-9
precepts.why:
Isaiah said the people draw near with their mouth and honour God with their lips, “but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men”. The precept of men is the doctrine of men.

Christ says the same thing and names who Isaiah was speaking of: “Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.”

The elders in Isaiah's day were teaching doctrines of men, and the Pharisees in Christ's time were doing the exact same thing. Those elders had children, and those children became the opposition of Christ in his time. The same spirit passed down.

So the doctrine of trinitarianism is exactly that: teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. It is not found plainly in the Bible; it comes from men. People draw near with their lips and argue about essence and substance while their heart is far from God and they forsake his laws, and in vain do they worship him.

thread.label: Isaiah 43:3-11
thread.text: For I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour: I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.

classes.title: The God Of War & Salvation

precepts.label: Revelation 18:4
precepts.why:
“I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.” The Lord gave other nations for us: he brought blood and destruction on their heads on our behalf. “Since thou wast precious in my sight”, not yellow, black and white all precious in his sight like the Christian song says, but the twelve tribes, “therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” He didn't say he would spare the little Arab kids or the Israeli kids planted in the land. Revelation shows how much he loves us in the middle of that.

He has put it in front of us in prophecy: what is about to go down, where it is going down, who is involved and who is conspiring against Israel, and the parts they will play. He has told us not to meddle with them, and he has told us what to do to secure our salvation.

“And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people.” Who are his people? According to Isaiah 3:12, children are their oppressors and women rule over them; only the southern kingdom and northern kingdom have that problem. So he is letting you know it is only Israel.

“That ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” Don't be part of the sins and the plagues coming on this place, the land of the north where Esau dwells, or in the valley of decision where everybody is gathering for the great day of Armageddon. Don't receive the death and destruction on the way when the Most High shows up.

So your fight is not with the nations. Your fight is with getting yourself together, working on your salvation, so you can see the promise made to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

precepts.label: Isaiah 3:12
precepts.why:
Isaiah 43 says, “Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee.” Who is the “thee” the Lord loves and gives other nations for? Revelation 18 says “Come out of her, my people”, and Isaiah 3 identifies who his people are.

“As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them.” There is only one people with that problem: the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom, Israel. We are the only ones living under it.

So “my people” is Israel, not all nations. The fools who want to engraft all the nations say, what about all nations? But if you acknowledge that we are the twelve tribes of Israel and still want to engraft every other nation in, when are you going to acknowledge that they have to give us back our land and everything that belongs to us? You won't. It's hypocrisy.

The Lord has not dealt with any other nation. “Even every one that is called by my name: for I have created him for my glory”, and “Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord.” All the destruction coming on the other nations is to set the twelve tribes of Israel, those keeping the commandments and striving, back in their rightful place.

thread.label: Isaiah 43:9
thread.text: Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the people be assembled: who among them can declare this, and shew us former things? let them bring forth their witnesses, that they may be justified: or let them hear, a

classes.title: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:20
precepts.why:
“Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the people be assembled: who among them can declare this, and shew us former things? let them bring forth their witnesses.” Who can show the things from the past? The next verse answers: “Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen.” God’s witnesses on this earth are the children of Israel, and the two sticks, the stick of Judah and the stick of Ephraim, the southern and northern kingdoms, are two witnesses also.

What does a witness have? A testimony. A witness testifies, like a witness to a crime in a court of law. And we do not play a small role. Isaiah shows what God’s witnesses testify: “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.”

As witnesses, what we are supposed to be testifying is the law and the testimony. If they do not speak according to this word, the law and the testimony, there is no light in them.

The testimony is what John bore record of: “the testimony of Jesus Christ, and of all things that he saw.” Part of that testimony is to identify “them which say they are Jews, and are not”, the synagogue of Satan. And Malachi’s testimony: “They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness.” The they who call them that are the witnesses, the prophets. So when the nations are gathered and asked for witnesses, Israel stands to the law and to the testimony.

precepts.label: Sirach 36:14
precepts.why:
“Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord.” A witness has a testimony. What is the testimony Israel carries? Sirach shows where it came from: “Fill Sion with thine unspeakable oracles, and thy people with thy glory: Give testimony unto those that thou hast possessed from the beginning, and raise up prophets that have been in thy name.”

The testimonies are what God gave to Moses, to Jeremiah, to Nahum, to Micah, to Isaiah, to Peter, Paul and the apostles. All the things these men wrote are the testimony: testimonies of things that are going to happen in the future, of what is going to happen to the children of Israel.

So when the scripture says the witnesses have to testify, the testimony is what is written, what the prophets said is going to happen. That is why Isaiah 43:9 asks “who among them can declare this, and shew us former things?” No other nation can. Israel, the people God possessed from the beginning, was given the unspeakable oracles, and we testify them.

And as we testify, we bring forth judgment. Brought before governors and kings “for a testimony against them and the Gentiles”, it is not we who speak but the Spirit of our Father speaking in us. The wicked who hides as an angel of light is revealed and condemned, because the witnesses must testify first before God brings forth judgment, as in a court of law.

thread.text: Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God.

precepts.label: Micah 2:11
precepts.why:
“Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine.” We are an afflicted people, and we haven’t realized it yet. We are being put through the wringer because we constantly break his law of commandments, because we departed from God, because we don’t know who we are, and because God has been calling us and we refuse to turn around and come back to him. And we are drunken, but not with wine. Drunken with what? Micah shows it.

“If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” We are drunk with philosophy and doctrines, the lies we learned here in America. If you follow those doctrines, those laws, those philosophies, those lies, that man is going to be the prophet to you: a prophet to lead you right to hell.

A lot of these wicked and evil pastors are just chasing money, money, money, and don’t give a damn about the people’s souls or their spirits. They don’t care about healing the people, fixing the people and bringing them back to Christ. The people are crying, looking for Christ, and these men mislead them while chasing the dollar bill. Let those men be your prophet if you are going to believe that garbage.

That is why we have gangs in the street, prostitutes in the street, our sons fainted and lying “at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”: the dead Israelites in the churches are not teaching our people how to keep the Lord’s commandments or how to come back to Christ. But the Lord who “pleadeth the cause of his people” says he has taken the cup of trembling out of our hand, and “I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee.”

thread.label: Isaiah 51:20
thread.text: Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God.

classes.title: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.label: Job 8:8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 51:20 says “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”. What other people on the planet are at the head of every corner on the streets? That's us: in Miami, in the Bronx, in all the hoods and all the ghettos throughout the whole earth. We fainted, we are hid in prison houses, and we are on every corner. They ignorantly call us YNs, and we call ourselves YNs, uncs and OGs, but that ain't your culture. Whatever happened to the ancients, the hoary head, the elders of our nation, the kings?

So the Lord says, “For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Prepare yourself for the search of your ancestors. When we bethink ourselves, we come back to our heritage and to knowing who we are. It is no longer, I'm a YN: we have young prophets amongst us. We are raising up our sons and daughters, young men, teens and young adults, in the understanding that they are the children of the prophets, the sons and daughters of God.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” What our fathers went through was written for our learning, to increase our faith. When you learn from the examples of our ancestors, it gives us a guide for how we need to be today. That's called legacy.

How did our ancestors handle famine, persecution and tribulation? Job lost his children and his wealth and was covered in boils, and he said, “the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” Abraham was called to go out and “went out, not knowing whither he went”, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob. We are going to have to get back to that, and who else did it but us? We are them; they are us.

thread.label: Isaiah 59:1-4
thread.text: Behold, the Lord’s hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear:

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:28
precepts.why:
“For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity.” Our hands in the black and brown community are defiled with blood. In Joliet a young man, twenty-three years old, shot to death his own mother, his aunt, his uncle, his bedridden brother and his three sisters, killed another man and shot one more, and then shot himself. That's trauma right there, and the law explains it: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.”

The Lord shall smite thee with madness: meaning our people are insane. No rhyme, no reason to what they do or why they do it. That's being smitten with madness. We have generational curses. Three teens on a thirty-hour spree of armed robberies and the murder of a churchgoing man; a woman charged with stabbing and killing a three-year-old boy, appearing in court laughing and smiling: that is stricken with madness.

The Bible says, thou shalt not kill, and we are not taught that in church, so some of us grow up with a hateful and murderous spirit on us. No matter how bad, insulting or degrading these videos are, they are filtered through the Bible, showing the stage and state of where we are today, and it is still proof that we are the children of Israel under the curses. The Bible ain't the white man's book. The Bible is our book.

That is why the Lord's hand is not shortened and his ear is not heavy, and still he does not save: “your iniquities have separated between you and your God.”

precepts.label: Revelation 13:9-10
precepts.why:
“None calleth for justice, nor any pleadeth for truth.” You might say, that's not right; our people are in the street all the time crying, no justice, no peace. But the justice our people want is called money. They don't want the justice of the Bible. Here is God's justice: “If any man have an ear, let him hear. He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.”

Now that's justice. And you know what our people say? No, you hate the white man. They know what the scripture means: the one who led into slavery going into slavery, the one who killed with the sword being put to death by the sword. And they say, no, we don't want that kind of justice. We want money, money, money.

That is Isaiah 59:4: none calling for God's justice. They cry for justice in the streets, but when the justice of God is read to them, they call it hateful.

precepts.label: Psalms 89:14
precepts.why:
“Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne: mercy and truth shall go before thy face.” God's throne is all about justice and judgment. That's exactly what the world doesn't want.

“nor any pleadeth for truth”: they are not pleading for God's truth. The families of our brothers and sisters put to death unjustly, Sandra Bland and the rest, want the truth regarding their case, but they don't want God's truth as a whole. We may march with them and support them, but there is no internal change: they are mad at the white man and still celebrating Christmas and the white man's holidays. “be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.” If I used to celebrate Easter, now I celebrate Passover. They are making a conscious effort not to change.

The Lord is coming with justice and judgment, the habitation of his throne. That is why the world, which cries for justice, will be angry when it comes.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:18
precepts.why:
Everybody says, I can't wait until Jesus comes back. Let's see what the Bible says: “And the nations were angry, and thy wrath is come.” All these nations, countries and religious organizations say they want the Messiah to return, and the Bible prophesies they will be angry.

Why are they angry? Because “Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne.” The Lord is coming with justice and judgment, and the nations don't want that. Many of those nations are living on stolen land, like America. This is stolen land. They are lying when they say they can't wait. Christ's wrath is coming; he's not coming to hand out lollipops and hugs and kisses.

“and the time of the dead, that they should be judged, and that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints, and them that fear thy name, small and great.” You know what that reward is? Power. He's going to give his servants power.

“and shouldest destroy them which destroy the earth.” That's them. They say the aerosols in the black and brown community are destroying the ozone layer, not their rockets and missiles. All that climate change global BS: they are the ones destroying the earth, digging up and sucking out the oil that is meant to lubricate the tectonic plates, and then they wonder why the earthquakes are happening. They know it, and that's why they will be angry at his return. None calleth for the justice of God.

thread.label: Isaiah 59:5-8
thread.text: They hatch cockatrice’ eggs, and weave the spider’s web: he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.label: Matthew 3:7-8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 59:5 says “They hatch cockatrice’ eggs”, and a cockatrice is like a poisonous snake. Put together everything from verses two to four, the iniquities that separated us from our God, the hands defiled with blood, the lips that have spoken lies, and this is what comes of it: “he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper.” The eggs that are crushed are the kids that come out: a little baby snake. They produce evil followers.

Many years ago at a community meeting a black woman screamed at the police that they were selling drugs in her building and nobody was doing anything. The police set up a sting and locked up two dudes putting drugs in the mailboxes: her own sons. Then she came back saying it was false, with them on video. These are the eggs, the snake eggs coming out.

John the Baptist saw the same thing: “But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers”. That is the same thing Isaiah was talking about. “who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”.

A generation of vipers cannot just say it repents. You have to bring forth God's commandments in application; that is what proves your repentance.

precepts.label: Matthew 12:34
precepts.why:
Now Christ is speaking to them: “O generation of vipers”. That goes back to Isaiah 59, the cockatrice' eggs that break out into a viper. Christ called them vipers, and John the Baptist called them vipers. And their children are little snakes too.

“how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.” What is in the heart comes out of the mouth. A generation of vipers cannot speak good things, because what fills their heart is evil.

That is Isaiah 59 again. Before verse 5, verse 3 said our lips have spoken lies and our tongue perverseness. The lips speak lies and the tongue perverseness because the heart is full of iniquity, and the eggs they hatch are the same kind as the ones who laid them.

precepts.label: Isaiah 65:2
precepts.why:
“I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts”. See what our people do: they walk after their own thoughts. They don't give a damn what the Bible says; I do what I want to do.

And their thoughts are the white man's thoughts. Our people follow all these man-made religions, and they don't teach God's laws, his commandments, his statutes. We ain't got to keep no laws, because that is what all these white people were teaching: don't keep no laws.

So what do you get? Those vipers hatch eggs, and what comes out? Little vipers, little snakes. Your son, little Tyrone, is a snake, and your daughter, little Chenique, was a snake too. That is what God is saying in Isaiah 59:5, and it is why verse 7 says “their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity”: a rebellious people walking after their own thoughts.

precepts.label: Job 8:13-15
precepts.why:
Isaiah 59 says they “weave the spider’s web” and “Their webs shall not become garments”. Job explains the spider's web. “So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite’s hope shall perish: Whose hope shall be cut off”, because they are hypocrites, “and whose trust shall be a spider’s web.”

Their trust shall be as a spider's web: you get tangled up in that thing, and that spider comes out and bites you and eats you up.

“He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.” Your house won't stand. A people who forget God weave their webs and lean on what they built, but it cannot cover them or hold them up. That is why Isaiah 59:6 goes on, “neither shall they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:1-2
precepts.why:
Isaiah 59:6 says “neither shall they cover themselves with their works”, and Isaiah 30 shows the covering they use instead. “Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me”: they are looking for counsel, but not from God. “and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit”, not according to the Bible, “that they may add sin to sin”.

“That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth”. At that time it was actual Egypt, but today it's America, spiritual Egypt. They have not asked the prophets what the Bible says. They go “to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!” America ain't the real Egypt, but it is the shadow of Egypt, and our people trust in it.

That is why the act of violence is in their hands. A cruise line banned passengers for life over a brawl in the buffet; graduation ceremonies break out into fights with families arrested, a day of celebration turned into chaos. Our people have made crooked paths for themselves, following the Democratic or the Republican party, the cross and the white Jesus, and whosoever goes therein shall not know peace.

thread.label: Isaiah 59:9-15
thread.text: Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us: we wait for light, but behold obscurity; for brightness, but we walk in darkness.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:29
precepts.why:
“We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noonday as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men.” We got eyes, but we act like we ain't got none. We act like what we just saw didn't happen. The curse said it would be so: “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.”

We are like blind people, but we have eyes. We see we're not prospering as a people. We see we're under constant oppression as a people. But we act like we don't see it, because oppression has become so normal to us; it's our everyday life.

It's high noon, but in our minds we are so spiritually blind it is like night for us. “we are in desolate places as dead men”: that's the black and brown community, desolate places, our people like the walking dead. Isaiah 59 is Deuteronomy 28:29 in real time.

That is why verse 9 says, “Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us.” We want to live filthy lives, evil lives, violent lives, and then expect justice from God. It don't work like that. Oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 11:12-13
precepts.why:
There is a difference between being spiritually slow and being spiritually dead. “we are in desolate places as dead men,” but Sirach shows what the nation needs: “Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty.” We usually read it as an individual, but think about it on a bigger scale. You might say this is Joe or Bob. No, this is us.

Slow, needing help, lacking ability, full of poverty: that is our people. “yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate,” and lifted up his head from misery, so that many that saw it marvelled at him.

The nations are going to marvel when God raises us up. It will be such a shock that this low, degenerate race of people is now going to rule the earth. We lack the ability now; it is the Lord's eye that sets us up from our low estate.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:20-21
precepts.why:
“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is the nation of Israel; think of it as whatever IUIC school you come from. Every camp leader, the head of the sanctuary, must be able to identify the gold brothers and the silver brothers, the gold sisters and silver sisters, and also look through the school and say, this brother and this sister is earth, this one is wood.

If you can't discern that, you'll have problems in the school, putting people in positions that don't fit them. Marcus Garvey had his ships and put his best friends over them, and they didn't know how to run a ship: one crashed, one went to his girlfriend's house, and he lost it all because of friendship. Shake the friendship appointments. Who is best qualified? Who knows what they're doing? A dummy who doesn't study set up as a school leader, and all hell breaks loose. If sanctuary leaders have no discernment, they are spiritually blind and destined for ruin.

Some brothers and sisters are just slow and need more time to grow. Fine; don't put them in that position yet if others are better qualified. “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work.” Purge yourself from the wood and earth spirits. They see this truth not as a government, not as the mustard seed of a government, but as a social club, dancing every new moon and confused when it comes to God's work. That is how a people groping like the blind becomes vessels unto honour.

precepts.label: John 3:18-21
precepts.why:
The voices of our people conceive and utter from the heart words of falsehood, lies on top of lies. Christ answers: “He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.” If you believe on the black Messiah, you are not condemned; if you believe not, you're not even keeping commandment one.

“And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Christ is that light that came into the world, and men love darkness, sin, rather than light, Christ and keeping the commandments. It didn't change from Isaiah to John; it's the same thing: “we wait for light, but behold obscurity.”

“For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.” They hate Christ, they hate keeping the laws, they hate the commandments, because if you come to Christ your deeds will be reproved: have no other gods before me, bow down to no graven image, remember the Sabbath, honour your father and your mama, thou shalt not kill. They don't want to hear that.

“But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.” We want Christ, the word of God, to make our deeds manifest. What am I? Lord, show me.

precepts.label: Amos 5:10
precepts.why:
“Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey.” If you depart from evil by repenting, you make yourself a prey to everybody around you; everybody around you hates your guts now. Amos says the same thing: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.”

That includes some of your own mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers. They hate the one who rebukes and abhor the one who speaks uprightly, because “truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter.”

“and the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.” There was no true judgment in the earth. The one who departs from evil is hated for it, and the Lord sees it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:16
precepts.why:
“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted.” He has chosen and set apart every man here, all the captains, to preach good tidings to the meek. But how do you bind up a person that is broken? The brokenhearted are broken in the mind: suffering the curses without knowing the will of God. We are set apart to bind them up. What do we bind them with?

“Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” We bind up the testimony and seal the law in the minds of the people, because they are brokenhearted and their minds are broken. That is what we are called to do: to bind them to the laws of God.

And we show them why it is good. Look at our lives as the example of what it means to serve God and why it is good to serve him. That means we have to be sincere about it. How do we tell the people to touch not the unclean thing and then not live it ourselves? The one who was profitable to many but not to himself will be punished accordingly, because he knew better.

So the good tidings we proclaim with the law are these: if we repent and keep God's laws in sincerity and endure to the end, he will deliver us, and we will rule again, as we were made in his image to rule.

precepts.label: Isaiah 49:1-8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 says to “proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord”, and Isaiah 49 says it again: “Thus saith the Lord, In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee: and I will preserve thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages.” The acceptable year and the acceptable time: that is when we heal the broken heart and proclaim liberty to the captives.

“The Lord hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name. And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me, and made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me; And said unto me, Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” We are supposed to glorify our God in this body.

“Then I said, I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain: yet surely my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God.” We go to stiff-necked, hard-hearted people who refuse to hear the word of God, but we still proclaim the day of the Lord to heal those minds and tell them there is an end to this: we will rule one day. He formed us from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him.”

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” It may not appear that we are doing it, but when the numbers come in, it is a light thing he has given us, and he still charges us to raise up the children of Israel. “I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth”: that goes back to Matthew 4, the Gentiles of Galilee. Our job is to bring salvation to the people and lead them back to him, and that is a great ministry.

“Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship” … “and he shall choose thee.” Out of all of them, he is going to choose us. And unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: we want to be the faithful servant the Lord finds doing this work in sincerity, without deceit and without secret sins.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 23:13-16
precepts.why:
When Ezekiel dug in the wall, he saw “every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.” That is like putting the images of Cesare Borgia on the walls, or Guadalupe on the walls, today. Ezekiel 23 shows what they were putting on the walls: images of the gods of their enemies.

“Then I saw that she was defiled, that they took both one way, And that she increased her whoredoms: for when she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion, Girded with girdles upon their loins, exceeding in dyed attire upon their heads, all of them princes to look to, after the manner of the Babylonians of Chaldea”. Israel looked at the pictures of her enemies on the wall, dressed up like princes.

“And as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea.” As soon as she saw them, she wanted them. That is why the Lord said in Numbers 15, when he gave us the fringes, that with your eyes you will go a whoring.

So the imagery on the walls of the temple in Ezekiel 8 was not harmless decoration. The images of other nations and their gods drew Israel's eyes, and her eyes drew her heart after them. It is the same today with the images hung on our walls, and it is why the Lord said, I cannot be around you all, and went far off from his sanctuary.

precepts.label: John 3:19
precepts.why:
Ezekiel was shown “what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.” Seventy elders with censers in their hands, burning incense to the images in the dark. What do they do in the dark? What do you do in the dark? Your secrets, your secret sins.

Christ gives the judgment on it: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men love the dark because their deeds are evil; they hide there because they think the Lord does not see them.

But the Lord brought Ezekiel through the hole in the wall to show him exactly what was done in the dark. Nothing done in the chambers of imagery is hidden from him. The ancients said the Lord had forsaken the earth, but it was they who had forsaken the light, and that is the condemnation.

thread.label: Ezekiel 16:44
thread.text: Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use this proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter.

classes.title: My Temple My Choice

precepts.label: Proverbs 22:6
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says the proverb will be used against us: “As is the mother, so is her daughter.” Very rarely do you see a fat mother and a skinny daughter. If the mama is big, the daughter is big, and if there is a son, he is really big too, because what you eat to get there is exactly what the kids have in the house to eat. The kid models himself or herself after the parents. If you are in the house working out, your kids will want to do push-ups and pull-ups and be in the gym with you. If you like to lie on the bed eating ice cream, they will lie in the bed eating ice cream with you. That self-hatred gets passed on, and that is how the cycle continues: grandmama's fat, mama's fat, the kid is fat, and they all give the same excuse, my thyroid, we big boned. Garbage.

So Proverbs gives the command: “Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” It is you that has to shape and mould the trajectory of the kid's life. That goes from teaching them the laws, to showing them what is good to eat and what is not good to eat, to showing them to exercise and to do their studies: train them in the right direction in every aspect.

If there is no candy in the house, can a six-year-old go outside and buy candy? Hell no. If there are no donuts in the house, can a six-year-old go and buy donuts? The kid eats what you feed them. And stop giving your kids choices: put sugary food and good food before a kid and ask what they want, and they will always choose sugar. A kid does not know. When your kid loves a healthy food, give it to them all the time.

If you are big and your kid is big, how will you feel when your young kid needs insulin shots because he is diabetic from being overfed on all kinds of garbage? Where is the love in that? Laziness is why a lot of the time we don't deal with our kids right and we don't deal with ourselves right. If we want to save our kids, it starts with you first: control your eating and exercise, and then you are setting the right example, so that the daughter who is as her mother is trained in the right way.

thread.text: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy chil

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears
2025 Recap: Different Times, Same Truth

precepts.label: Exodus 19:6
precepts.why:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me”. What does that part mean, that thou shalt be no priest to me?

There was a promise made to us and our ancestors: “And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.” A kingdom of priests. That is what Israel was called to be.

Go back to Hosea and it tells you why we lost it: “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God”. That is the knowledge. Usually we jump over to Malachi 2:7, but the verse tells you right there: the knowledge is the law of God, his laws, his commandments, his statutes. Because we forgot it, he rejected us from that priesthood.

That is why we are destroyed as a race, as a people, mentally and spiritually. The twelve tribes of Israel are a destroyed race. This is why other races come into our communities and run the hospitals, the stores, the clinics. The black man and the brown man do have the ability, and many of us have the knowledge to do it, but they do not want us to have the capabilities.

precepts.label: Malachi 2:7
precepts.why:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge”. What is the knowledge we have rejected? Malachi answers: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth”. The knowledge is the law.

So the knowledge is not what you learn at a university; the black woman is the most educated woman on the earth, and that is not the knowledge we are ignorant of. Our people are ignorant of the laws of God. Our people don't understand that today is the Lord's Sabbath, and you are not supposed to be buying and selling, cooking, or playing football, because the white man said every day is the Sabbath. Our women don't understand they are not supposed to wear pants, because that knowledge was taken from them. Our men in America don't know they are not supposed to shave their beards, because the white man said, if you want to look like a man, shave your beard.

We are in a diabolical matrix, deeper than anything the movie could show: everything you were taught is good here in America is bad. That is why Hosea goes on, “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.” That is what has happened to us. Our people are at the bottom of society, the mother with her kids living all year for a tax return, the drug dealers, the ball players and the rappers, all in Esau's trick bag, while the man down the street teaching the law is what would disrupt all of it.

precepts.label: Luke 16:15
precepts.why:
Everything the white man taught us is good here is bad. If you really want to go all out for your wife or your girlfriend, you buy lobster, the delicacy. The Bible says that is the scum of the earth. They have you paying $200 for a fat roach, eating clams and clam chowder, bottom feeders, rodents of the sea, and spending your hard-earned check to do it. You want to upscale a burger, put bacon on it. All of these things are abominable to God, and God is looking at us like, they have you in a trick bag. We are living in the upside-down.

Christ said it: “Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.” That which is highly esteemed among men is everything Esau and the nations put above God.

Justifying yourselves before men is the brothers and sisters who know the truth, who know what we are saying is right and will even say Jesus is black, but won't serve God, won't come out of the pagan holidays, and won't keep the commandments. God knows the heart.

That is how our people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. We have taken what men esteem, the Sunday, the shaved face, the shellfish and the bacon, over the law of our God, and calling a bottom feeder a delicacy makes absolutely no sense. The knowledge we rejected is the laws of God.

precepts.label: Amos 5:15
precepts.why:
Amos shows an Israel that hates the righteous: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.” They tread upon the poor, build houses of hewn stone and plant pleasant vineyards, “but ye shall not dwell in them”. Don't be comfortable, family; that is what Amos is saying. A few verses on he tells them what to hate instead: “Hate the evil, and love the good”.

David said, I love thy commandments, and I hate every false way. We hate anything outside of keeping God's commandments: sin. We are supposed to hate sin, hate the fact that there is sin in our community, and do something about it by keeping God's law. We are not supposed to tolerate evil amongst our people.

Love the good is love God's commandments. That is your purpose, it is what increases your faith, and it is why you are called to magnify God's law.

“And establish judgment in the gate”: establish judgment in yourself, your household, your nation and your communities. Then “it may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph.” You receive mercy when you hate the evil and love the good. That is the turn Amos calls for: stop hating the one who rebukes in the gate, and hate the sin instead. We separate ourselves from evil, the ways of our oppressor, and we strive for perfection.

precepts.why:
Amos says, “And though they go into captivity before their enemies, thence will I command the sword, and it shall slay them”. Who is the sword? The wicked at the time. David shows it: “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”, and he goes on, “From men which are thy hand, O Lord”.

God wields the wicked as his sword. The wicked today is the United States. He is going to use them to bring in all these wars you are seeing, and we have to get right.

That is why we can't bug out or get caught up in everything going on. Nobody wants to see Arab children losing limbs; nobody wants to see destruction. But we understand why it is happening, and we understand what we have to do, so that when the final war comes, he that endureth to the end shall be saved. That is what we want: deliverance.

So it was with us. The twelve tribes went into captivity after captivity before our enemies, because God allowed every bit of it. He commanded the sword and it slew us, and he set his eyes upon us “for evil, and not for good”, because we did not keep the commandments. The Iranians don't get a pass; they had us in captivity too, as did the princes of Ishmael. There is slavery happening right now in parts of Africa, and it is not Black Americans or Israelites running it, but Arabs and Caucasians with financial power. Wars are here: seek good and not evil.

precepts.label: Isaiah 46:10
precepts.why:
Amos says “the Lord God of hosts is he that toucheth the land”. When Iran is being touched right now, and Israel, the Lord is involved in all of it; by his counsel the land gets touched. Isaiah shows that counsel: “Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done”.

This is the power we have: understanding that the Most High God from the very beginning planned every war, including the third world war to come. Ancient times means way back when Adam and Eve walked. From then he declared it. As his sons and daughters, the Israelites, we have to know our Father has this covered and his Son is coming back. Right now we have to rehearse the righteous acts and get right.

That is how we can make the bold statement that God is behind the Israelis doing what they do in the US government, and behind the Iranians spending twenty years building huge, elaborate tunnel systems and storing munitions and advanced rocketry. All of it was set up from ancient times. They send drones that cost fifteen to twenty thousand dollars, and the other side fires interceptor missiles that cost a million or more to take them out. You see how they will not be able to keep up. God put all that in these leaders.

“My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure”. It was his pleasure when we went into chattel slavery, through Jim Crow and through civil rights. We had to learn the lesson.

Jeremiah shows the same counsel: “Therefore hear ye the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Babylon”. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: Israel, the least of Esau's flock, draws the United States out into the Middle East, and “At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved”. Amos lived way before anything could melt the land. Today thermonuclear ICBMs can, and it is all by his counsel.

precepts.label: Sirach 25:1
precepts.why:
“In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.” The Lord puts the unity of brethren first. Then the love of neighbours: the charity, the long-suffering.

Then “a man and a wife that agree together.” Agree on what? The commandments. That is not talking about arguing over the curtains. Brother, when did you become a fashion designer, an interior decorator? Let your wife handle that. The agreement God counts beautiful is agreement in keeping his law.

This is what the gathering of Zephaniah 2:1 has to look like. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: the nation hated upon the earth has to come together in the last days. But as we gather, we have to fix our character flaws, show ourselves friendly, and endeavor to keep the unity, and endeavor is an enduring word, not one to be taken lightly.

Unity of brethren does not mean you cannot correct one another or admonish one another. It means you expect highly of each other. We need correction, admonishment, counsel and advice amongst each other. Those who push you toward hard things, who tell you the harsh truth when a lie would be easier, are your people. That is how the gathered nation stands up beautiful before God and men.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:17
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.” Love for one another means we are not supposed to suffer sin on one another.

So if I see my brother or my sister in the midst of sin, I might have to give them that rough talk. And it is to do what? To put them back in the righteous mindset. Real admonishment and love, being able to correct your brothers, comes with a little bit of hard criticism. You cannot take it emotionally, and you cannot take it personally. Tell the brother he is fat: fix it, brother. That is love, not hate.

Friends who roast each other are the loyal ones; those who value your success over the need to be liked are the ones who truly want your best. Their words are heavy, but their loyalty is pure. Don’t think that because a man is charitable he doesn’t correct anybody. We have to stop thinking with that emotional Christianity.

This is how the nation of Zephaniah 2:1 gathers. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: in the last days we gather with the believers who fear the Lord, and until we receive our homeland we are all we got. Rebuking one another in love keeps the gathered body clean and keeps the unity.

precepts.label: Luke 3:23-24
precepts.why:
Matthew 1 is “The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham”: the link between Christ and the royal seat promised through David's loins, through Solomon and their sons. At the end of it: “Eliud begat Eleazar; and Eleazar begat Matthan; and Matthan begat Jacob; And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary”. Someone claimed Jacob and Heli were brothers. You do not read that anywhere in the Bible.

Luke 3: “And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli”. Did it say the son of Heli? No. “As was supposed” refers to him being the son of Joseph. It had nothing to do with Heli at all.

Now line them up. Luke goes on: “Which was the son of Matthat, which was the son of Levi, which was the son of Melchi”. Even if Matthat and Matthan were the same man spelled differently, Matthan's father in Matthew is Eleazar, and in Luke Matthat's father is Levi. Eliud and Eleazar are not mentioned in Luke 3 at all. These are two completely different bloodlines. They do not expect you to bounce back and forth and make sure it lines up; they bank on you not fact-checking.

Matthew starts with Joseph: the angel comes to Joseph, you follow his story, and his lineage is given. Luke chose to follow Mary: it begins with her cousin Elisabeth and the babe leaping in her womb, and in the third chapter it gives her lineage, all men. That is why not one woman is named in Luke 3, while some women are named in Matthew 1. Where it would have said Mary, it names her husband.

And “Booz begat Obed of Ruth” is where the levirate marriage actually shows up, but we will not be bamboozled by a spin move into an Old Testament law that has nothing to do with the question. Not knowing something does not make you an idiot. Pick up the phone and ask a Bishop or a Deacon. Making it up does.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:36-37
precepts.why:
Christ walked by the sea of Galilee and said to Peter and Andrew, “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” Baruch shows where that invitation comes from.

“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” All the understanding and wisdom was given to us, not to the other nations. So there is no reason for you to sit on that wisdom and do nothing.

“Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.” That is speaking of Christ. We are the only ones that have a God; the other nations do not. Our God saw us as so special that he showed himself on the earth. Our God, Emmanuel, walked with us and conversed with us. That goes back to Matthew 4 when he said “Follow me”: that was our leader telling us to follow him.

So we are not supposed to just sit here and do absolutely nothing. Our God saw fit to walk with us, teach us and guide us, and we have to do the same thing: teach our brothers and sisters and wake them up. The invitation is there, and like Peter and Andrew, who “straightway left their nets, and followed him”, we have to accept it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 49:5-6
precepts.why:
This is our job. “And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him”. You were made to be the servant of God. You were made to do this work. You were not born to be a basketball player or a rapper. You were born to be a servant of God; that is our duty and our calling. “To bring Jacob again to him”: that is your commission.

“Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.”

“And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”. Think about that: it is a light thing. It is the least you can do. The Lord sacrificed himself for you; our God came down and walked with us. It is a light thing to do the work of the Lord and go wake up your people.

“I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.” That is the same thing read in Matthew 4: Galilee of the Gentiles, the people that sat in darkness, saw great light. It is talking about Israel; we are to go to our brothers of the Northern Kingdom and be the light to the Gentiles, carrying on the mission God gave us.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:14
precepts.why:
“Ye are the light of the world.” Not the light of Brooklyn, not the light of one city: of the world. When the Lord sent us out, he sent us out as a light to the whole world, and Matthew 24 shows how far that light has to go.

“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” How is it going to be preached in all of the world if you have no plans, no plan of action, no implementation to do anything worldwide? How are you the guys if you ain't got global goals and you ain't touching the ends of the earth?

The Lord sent his prophets with vision, with goals, with aspirations to take it to the ends of the earth. That is why leadership puts things in place: “Where there is no vision, the people perish.” This is a global mission, and our aspirations and goals have to be set to a global standard, not a local one.

So the light of the world is a people carrying the gospel of the kingdom to all nations, and the end does not come until that witness has gone out.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:11
precepts.why:
“The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” Our people are the remnant, scattered to the four corners of the world.

How are these people going to be able to rise out of these places if they were never told? That is why this gospel has to have a global standard, preached to the whole world. If your leadership ain't talking about covering the earth, they're not the guys. Don't waste your time.

They ridicule us now: y'all going over there to Africa, y'all in India, you went to Australia, you went to Papua New Guinea. We don't give a damn how anybody feels about it. Negro, you do lack the understanding of this Bible; you do err, not knowing the scriptures. The people have been scattered to the four corners. How are you going to reach them if your aspirations are just down the street, if you want to be known for Times Square or a street corner?

Where would we be today if this truth had stayed in Harlem, if it never left the streets of Brooklyn? Where a lot of these other camps are. Being the light of the world means going where the remnant was scattered, to the islands of the sea, and telling them who they are.

precepts.label: Luke 1:6
precepts.why:
Christ said to men, “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” The trinity doctrine says no: only God can keep the commandments, so Christ cannot be fully a man, because a full man can't keep those laws, but a full man and a full God can. The insidiousness behind it is to make it impossible for man to keep God's commandments.

Luke answers that with John the Baptist's parents, Zacharias and Elisabeth: “And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.” Both righteous. Walking in all the commandments. Blameless: that's perfect. So human beings can keep God's commandments, perfect as the Father in heaven. It can be done.

The scripture also says we are gods but shall die like men, so we are the two anyway; for not keeping the commandments we die like men.

Peel back the layers of confusion and the doctrine is all about removing the humanity of Christ, or keeping some of it and making him a god too, so that man can't keep the commandments: Christ kept the laws so we don't have to do anything. That's the whole premise behind the great swelling words. “The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin”: their sport is not having to keep the commandments. Where is Christmas, New Year, Halloween, carnival, Labor Day, the Fourth of July or birthdays in the Bible? Your three-in-one God has nothing to say about them.
