thread.label: 2 Thessalonians 2:3
thread.text: Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;

classes.title: Woe to Amerikkka

precepts.label: John 8:32
precepts.why:
“For that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition.” The falling away was us going into captivity and being cut off from our heritage. The last thing that has to happen is the revealing of the man of sin. That is why they do not want the true history of America taught: when it is taught, people look at him and say, that is the devil incarnate. When Ghana brought a resolution to the UN naming slavery the worst genocide ever, America would not even vote for it, because he will not admit his cruelty. The angels are activated as this truth is taught, and America is being made to show its hands.

The man of sin is a liar from birth. The Tuskegee study promised free health care to black men in Alabama and watched them go blind and die of syphilis for forty years, withholding penicillin even after it was discovered. And the biggest lie of all: you are a Gentile. No, we are Israelites.

That is where John 8:32 comes in: “And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” We do not follow his lies anymore. No Christmas, no 4th of July, no Valentine’s Day, no birthdays, nothing he prescribes. We follow the Bible, because the only truth there is, is in the Bible. If you do not follow this Bible, you are a slave.

No empire will sit back while you expose it. This is war against the most sadistic men ever to walk the earth: men who threw babies in the air in Haiti to cut them in half for sport, buried men to the neck under molasses for the ants, and fed pregnant women to dogs; and Epstein Island shows he has not changed. Christ said the next time he meets that man he will not meet him as a man. Our weapon against him is this book and this truth, and we cannot be lollygagging and playing with it.

thread.label: 2 Thessalonians 2:7
thread.text: For the mystery of iniquity doth already work: only he who now letteth will let, until he be taken out of the way.

classes.title: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.label: Luke 21:15
precepts.why:
“For the mystery of iniquity doth already work”: that is Rome, already working in the apostles’ time, “until he be taken out of the way.” “And then shall that Wicked be revealed.” Why does the wicked need to be revealed? Because he does not present himself as the wicked. He has transformed into an angel of light, into Lucifer, and people think he is the righteous. But God’s witnesses, the Israelites, the prophets that are waking up, will testify who the wicked is and reveal him: the so-called white man, the nation of Edom, the people God hates. For years we have said it and many did not believe; now he is showing you who he is.

Then: “whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming.” Two things: consuming him with the spirit of his mouth, and destroying him with the brightness of his coming. What is the spirit of his mouth?

“For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.” That mouth and wisdom is Christ speaking through us, the Holy Spirit dwelling in us, so that nobody can gainsay us. That is the kind of power the Lord has given us.

So as we teach the word of God, the wicked are being consumed with the spirit of the Lord’s mouth, because we are bringing forth judgment. The Lord speaks through His witnesses, and their testimony condemns the wicked before his destruction at the brightness of Christ’s coming.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:18
precepts.why:
“And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.” We are going to be brought before governors and kings as a testimony against them. The testimony is us teaching the Bible, the laws and the testimonies, letting them know: God is coming back to destroy you. You are wicked. You have been stealing land, you have been murdering, you are the wicked of the earth.

When you testify on this earth, you are condemning people. Everybody who hears the word of God and turns their back on it is condemned. Every white person hearing about the Israelites and hearing these teachings, many of them online, is hearing that the Lord is going to judge Edom and judge Amalek, and those who call themselves Jews and are not. We are bringing forth judgment on the earth.

“But when they deliver you up, take no thought how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak. For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.” Do not worry what to say before kings. It will not be you speaking; the spirit that dwells in us takes over, and it is the Lord judging them with your voice.

That is how the Lord consumes the wicked “with the spirit of his mouth.” 2 Esdras 11 shows it too: the roaring lion that sends out a man’s voice unto the eagle, which is Rome, with Europe and America as its extension. That voice is the prophets, the witnesses on the earth today, condemning Edom for all the evil he has done through the centuries.

thread.text: Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils;

classes.title: My Temple My Choice

precepts.label: Psalms 119:142
precepts.why:
Christians take this chapter and say every creature is good to eat, so long as you pray over it. But Paul says the meats God created are “to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.” So what is the truth? “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The truth is the law.

That changes the whole verse. The meat is not received by everybody who bows his head over his plate. It is received by them that know the law. People say, just give thanks, just pray on it, and it's all right. Then can I pray on a human's foot and eat it? Pork carries the worm that lives in the muscle and can go to your brain; the shrimp, the lobster, the catfish and all the shellfish are bottom feeders whose job is to clean the ocean, the roaches of the sea. A prayer does not change what they are.

“For every creature of God is good” means what Genesis means: “God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good to serve its purpose. Worms prepare the land for planting, but we don't eat worms. The pig was the garbage disposal before there were trucks to pick up the garbage. Good for its work, not for your plate.

And Paul finishes: “For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” A Christian never reads up to that verse. The word of God is the law, the truth, and the law is what tells you which creatures are sanctified to eat. Many who have come into the truth, who know Christ is black and that we are Israel, are still struggling with that pork and that shrimp. This is the answer to that struggle: the ones who receive it with thanksgiving are those who know the law.

precepts.label: Sirach 32:24
precepts.why:
Paul says the meats are received “of them which believe and know the truth.” What is it to believe? “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment”. If you take heed to the commandments, you believe. Does a Christian believe in the commandments? So when he says you can eat anything as long as you receive it with thanksgiving, no: you can pray all you want, but you don't believe and you don't know the truth. Those are the very things that can save your life.

Finish the verse: “and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” If you believe in the commandments and keep the dietary laws, will you be worrying about high blood pressure? Will you be worrying about a foot amputation because of diabetes, about high cholesterol, about gout that takes brothers' fingers and feet? No, because you are not eating in a way where those sicknesses can come your way. The law tells you the food you can eat and the food you cannot eat.

All of that comes because people wanted to eat nasty, dirty food the Lord said don't eat. So take heed to yourself. Believing is not a prayer said over the plate; it is taking heed to the commandment, and the one who does fares never the worse.

precepts.label: Leviticus 11:46
precepts.why:
Paul says the meat “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” So where were the animals sanctified to be eaten or not to be eaten? In the law.

Leviticus 11 closes: “For I am the Lord your God: ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He repeats it: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” How do you become holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. To sanctify yourself and be holy you have to apply the law, the statutes and the commandments.

Then: “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.” This law takes in all the animals, whether they live on the earth or in the waters. That is how the word sanctifies the meat: by making a difference between what can be eaten and what cannot. Some animals are clean, some are unclean. It is basic.

The churches don't want you to learn the Old Testament, because they don't want you to be saved. “Keep my commandments, and live”. If you don't keep the law you are not going to live. John says “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food is sin; eating pork is going to kill you, and overeating is going to kill you.

You are supposed to be the temple of God. If you keep destroying yourself with the way you eat, you are working against what the Lord says, and against the work we are all called here to do. The meat that is received with thanksgiving is the meat the law sanctified.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:17-18
precepts.why:
Christ answered Peter, “Blessed art thou, Simon Bar–jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.” Then he told him, “thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.”

How do you think that made Peter feel? Christ telling you, I am going to build my church upon you. That is what great leaders do. Good leaders make you believe in them; great leaders make you believe in you. They empower others, they strengthen others, they make you believe in yourself and not in them.

That is how a leader transfers his belief onto others, the faith Hebrews 13:7 tells us to follow. It is how the Bishop is able to raise up other bishops, raise up deacons, raise up captains, and soldiers by the thousands. Great leaders raise up more leaders.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 3:25-28
precepts.why:
Moses prayed, “I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon. But the Lord was wroth with me for your sakes, and would not hear me”. He was told, “Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter”, and to go up to the top of Pisgah and behold the land with his eyes, “for thou shalt not go over this Jordan.”

Moses could not cross over, but look at what he was charged to do: “But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him: for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which thou shalt see.” Charge him, encourage him, strengthen him.

That is your job as a leader: to encourage and strengthen the men around you. A leader transfers his belief onto the next man, so that the one coming after him can lead the people into what he himself was given to see. That is part of the faith that those who have the rule over you pass on.

precepts.label: Job 4:3
precepts.why:
“Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” Your job as a leader is to instruct many. And your job is to strengthen the weak hands.

It is your job to build the brothers and the sisters up in the spirit. That is part of how a leader transfers his belief onto others: those who have the rule over you and have spoken unto you the word of God instruct you, and when your hands are weak they strengthen them, so that you can follow their faith.

precepts.label: Luke 22:32
precepts.why:
Christ told Peter, “But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” When you convert, strengthen your brothers. That is the charge that goes with the faith that is passed on to you.

Read on and Peter answers, “Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death”, and Christ answers that before the cock crows Peter will thrice deny that he knows him. Christ prayed that Peter's faith would not fail, knowing what was coming, and still gave him the work of strengthening his brethren.

This is the leader transferring his belief onto others. Christ imparted his faith to Peter, and Peter was to impart it to the brethren. The one who has been strengthened turns around and strengthens the next man.

precepts.label: Acts 18:23
precepts.why:
“And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.” Paul went country to country strengthening all the disciples. That is the job of a leader, and it shows how a leader transfers his belief onto others.

The same work goes on today. As the bishops and the deacons trailblazed the way, the captains follow the same path, and when they go to these places they continue to build our people up worldwide. A captain just back from Guyana reports that the brothers and sisters there in South America are growing tremendously, doing real good. The Lord has good things for them.

Like Paul in Galatia and Phrygia, the leaders go out to the nations where our people are and strengthen the disciples there.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 4:17
precepts.why:
“Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known”. The Lord stood with Paul and strengthened him, so that the preaching might go forth by him.

That is our job: we must strengthen one another. You get weak at different times. You need counsel. You need some exhortation. You have to vent sometimes. And it is your job as a leader to be there to strengthen each other, as the Lord stood with Paul.

So those who have the rule over you and speak the word of God unto you are there to strengthen you, and when you are strengthened, you follow their faith and do the same for those around you.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 3:8-9
precepts.why:
This is the rebuilding of Jerusalem. “Next unto him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths. Next unto him also repaired Hananiah the son of one of the apothecaries, and they fortified Jerusalem unto the broad wall.” Each man repaired his own section of the wall. Then: “And next unto them repaired Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler of the half part of Jerusalem.” The ruler of the half part: he was a supervisor over that area.

That is leadership. When you come in the truth you may just edit the video, go on the fly mission, or work in the kitchen. At some point you become over the office: now you are over the brothers that are editing, over the IT team, over the building team, over the sisters. Now your job changes, because you have people under you. Everybody is not built for that level. You are not in charge; you are responsible for those in your charge. In IUIC there are different offices with leads in place, and a man who was once responsible for one office, the Lord entrusted him with more.

Sometimes brothers get overwhelmed, and that will happen. But there is no better thing than to be overwhelmed for the Lord. You do not have a demon on your back, you are not behind bars, you are not suffering illness; you are stressed out for the Lord's work, and that is a beautiful thing. So do not complain. Come up and say, I need more assistance in this office. Pray and fast for more laborers, and rejoice in it, because the Lord gave you that office and put you in that position.

precepts.label: Romans 13:8-10
precepts.why:
James 2:8 says “If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well.” What is the royal law? Romans 13 lays it out.

“Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.” What law? Love your neighbour as yourself. “For this, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Thou shalt not covet”: every one of those is the royal law. “And if there be any other commandment”, any other commandment regarding your neighbour outside of those, “it is briefly comprehended in this saying, namely, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.”

Love your neighbour as yourself is an abbreviation of the six commandments. Of the ten spoken commandments, the first four are how you observe God, and the last six are how you serve your neighbour: honour your father and mother, don’t commit adultery, don’t kill, don’t steal, don’t bear false witness, don’t covet. Those six are briefly comprehended in that one saying. The ten spoken commandments were themselves an abbreviation.

“Love worketh no ill to his neighbour”: no ill like being a respecter of persons, seating the man with the gold ring in a good place and telling the poor man to stand over there. “Therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.” Do we keep it? Yes, you simple Christians. That is the royal law James is talking about, and respect of persons is sin against it.

precepts.label: Matthew 22:34-40
precepts.why:
“But when the Pharisees had heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, they were gathered together.” Christ had put the Sadducees to shame, and the Pharisees saw how sharp he was. “Then one of them, which was a lawyer, asked him a question, tempting him.”

A lawyer is a scribe. Their job was writing the Bible over and over again, because ink fades and animal skin and paper rip and smear, so it had to be copied again and again. They were the recorders and copyists, and they knew the law and the prophets off top. That is why he was tempting Christ: he already knew the answer. “Master, which is the great commandment in the law?”

“Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment.” That is the first four of the ten spoken commandments. “And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” That is the six, the royal law of James 2:8.

“On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.” These two are an abbreviation of all the laws. Loving God with all your heart, soul and mind means keeping the Sabbath day holy, the Passover, Tabernacles, Pentecost, the new moons, keeping the congregation, and the dietary law: don’t drink blood, don’t eat pork or shrimp. That is all serving God. The ten are an umbrella over all of them.

precepts.label: Mark 12:28-33
precepts.why:
Mark gives the same account with more detail, and it ties into sacrifice. “And one of the scribes came.” In Matthew he is called a lawyer; in Mark he is called a scribe, because they wrote things over and over and had the law in their minds. There were a bunch of them, but he was bold and spoke up: “Which is the first commandment of all?”

“The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord”: that is Deuteronomy 6:4. “And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment.” The commandments, the dietary law, the civil law, the sacrificial law, all of that is in there. “And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.” If you can keep those, you can keep them all.

“Well, Master, thou hast said the truth”: true, true, true. Then verse 33: “to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbour as himself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.” It is better than sacrifices. That is why Mark is loved: he makes it clear.

Why is it more than sacrifices? Because Israel would mess around, offer sacrifices, and then hate their neighbour, kill their neighbour, steal from their neighbour, bang their neighbour’s wife or sleep with their neighbour’s husband, but offer the best animal. The Lord said, I don’t care about that stuff. I care about your obedience, loving each other, loving me above the animals.

precepts.label: Sirach 35:1-3
precepts.why:
Mark 12:33 said loving God and your neighbour is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices. Ecclesiasticus 35 says the same.

“He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.” Keeping the law is offering enough.

“He that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour.” Under the offerings, you offered an animal, or fine flour if you were poor. Here, requiting a good turn, which is loving your neighbour as yourself, is the fine flour. “And he that giveth alms sacrificeth praise.”

“To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.” Propitiation means mercy, reconciliation. Departing from wickedness toward your neighbour is what reconciles you to God, which is why the royal law of James 2:8 stands above the sacrifices.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:22
precepts.why:
Saul disobeyed a direct order, and through Samuel the Lord asks him a question: “Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord?” Answer it.

“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” The Lord cared about obedience more than animal sacrifices.

That is the same point as Mark 12:33, that loving God and your neighbour “is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.” Saul wanted to bring the sacrifice after he had disobeyed; Israel wanted to bring the best animal after they had wronged their neighbour. The Lord wants the obedience. And that is why James 2 holds us to the royal law, love thy neighbour as thyself, and not to an offering that covers over a sin against the brother.

precepts.label: Psalms 40:6
precepts.why:
“Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.” This is quoted again in Hebrews 10.

David is saying, you opened my ears, and I understand the spirit: you don’t really care about sacrifices. Remember David wanted to build the temple. But the spirit was revealed to him that the sacrifices were just a placeholder for Christ to show up. He learned that because Christ was speaking through him.

So David realized: you don’t care about sacrifices at all, you care about obedience. That is what Samuel told Saul when he was king, “to obey is better than sacrifice.” And it is why the royal law of James 2, loving the neighbour and not being a respecter of persons, is what God is looking for.

precepts.label: Proverbs 21:3
precepts.why:
“To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.”

To do justice and judgment, just like the Lord told Saul to do, is more acceptable than sacrifice. He says it over and over and over again: in Samuel, in the Psalms, in Mark, and here in Proverbs.

Justice and judgment is how you treat your neighbour. In James 2 the assembly seated the rich man in a good place and told the poor man to stand there, and James asks, “Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” That is the opposite of doing justice and judgment, and no sacrifice would make up for it. Keeping the royal law is what is acceptable to the Lord.

precepts.label: Hosea 6:5-6
precepts.why:
“Therefore have I hewed them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of my mouth.” The word of God can slay; it is the spirit. “And thy judgments are as the light that goeth forth.”

“For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.” He was not about the sacrifice. That was a schoolmaster, a placeholder. He desired mercy and the knowledge of God.

The Lord eventually said away with it, through the prophets themselves. And that is where James 2:13 lands: “For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.” You shall receive no mercy if you show no mercy. Mercy rejoices against judgment: the Most High chooses to have mercy rather than to judge you for violating the royal law, and he looks for that same mercy in us toward our neighbour.

precepts.label: Judith 16:16
precepts.why:
“For all sacrifice is too little for a sweet savour unto thee, and all the fat is not sufficient for thy burnt offering: but he that feareth the Lord is great at all times.”

All sacrifice is too little. He that fears the Lord is great at all times. The Lord is saying, sacrificing, I don’t care about that; fearing me and obeying me is more important.

That closes the line of scriptures: Mark 12:33, Ecclesiasticus 35, 1 Samuel 15:22, Psalms 40:6, Proverbs 21:3, Hosea 6:6 and Judith 16:16 all say the same thing. Then back to James 2. “For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.” Christians use this to say that if you sin in one law you break them all, so you can’t keep them at all. But the context is the royal law, love your neighbour as yourself, and James explains it himself: “For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill.” If you commit no adultery but you kill your brother, you are a transgressor of the royal law.

“So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.” Under the old covenant, if you violated the moral law, moved your neighbour’s landmark or slept with your brother’s wife, you got death. Christ redeemed us from that and put us under the law of liberty. So stop doing it.

thread.text: What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?

classes.title: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 9:7
precepts.why:
“Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.” People say the law can’t save you, you are not justified by the works of the law. Ezra answers it: “And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by faith, whereby ye have believed.”

Everyone that shall be saved shall escape by what? His works. And by faith. Works and faith go hand in hand; you have to have both, as James said. You will be saved by both: not faith alone and no works, not faith and no commandments, not commandments and no faith. That makes no sense; it is dead, being alone.

“though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?” That is like a man saying I got a paycheck, with no job. I get paid tomorrow. You got a job? No. It is the dumbest thing you can say out of your mouth. Your faith proves your works and your works prove your faith. Abraham had faith and kept the commandments of God, and his keeping the commandments proved his faith.

And it goes back to the royal law, loving your neighbour as yourself. Telling a brother with no food and no clothes “be ye warmed and filled”, and giving him nothing, makes no damn sense. Even so, faith without works makes no sense: the faith does not exist.

precepts.label: Revelation 14:12
precepts.why:
“shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.” You cannot show faith without works. You show your faith through your actions, which is keeping the commandments of God. John says it in Revelation: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

Keep the commandments, and the faith of Jesus. The faith is one, and the commandments are the works. That is what James said, and what Ezra said: saved by works and by faith.

“Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.” Even the devils, the unclean spirits, believe in God and are afraid of him. “But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?” The vain man is the Christianity follower: faith without works, Calvinism, Protestantism, Catholicism. The saints are marked by both, the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus, and one without the other is dead.

precepts.label: Revelation 22:14
precepts.why:
The saints “keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus”, and Revelation shows what the commandments are for: “Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.”

That do his commandments: deeds, actions, works. They must do the commandments to enter in through the gates, and have faith in Christ. They go hand in hand.

That is James’ point: “Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.” A man who says he has faith but does no works, who will not keep the commandments, has no right to the tree of life. Christ redeemed us from the death that came from breaking the law, and put us under the law of liberty, “So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.” The doing is what gives the right to enter the city.

precepts.label: Romans 4:3
precepts.why:
“Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?” Abraham was justified by his works because his works proved his faith. Offering Isaac was his action. “Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?” His faith was perfected by his works; he was proven faithful by them.

“And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness.” That is the scripture Paul quotes in Romans 4: “Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.” The same belief Paul speaks of is the belief James says was fulfilled when Abraham laid his son on the altar. His belief was counted for righteousness, and his works showed that belief to be real, “and he was called the Friend of God.”

So Paul and James do not disagree. “Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only”, which goes back to Romans 2:13, that the doers of the law shall be justified. Abraham believed, and kept the commandments of God, and both went together.

precepts.label: Galatians 3:6
precepts.why:
James says “the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.” Paul quotes the same scripture to the Galatians: “Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.”

Abraham’s belief was accounted for righteousness, and James shows how it was fulfilled: when he offered Isaac his son upon the altar. “Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?” Faith worked together with his actions, and his actions perfected it.

“Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.” Rahab the harlot was justified the same way. She believed that if she helped the spies escape, they would spare her life; that was her faith, and receiving the messengers and sending them out another way was her works. “For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.” We have to keep the commandments and the faith of Christ; each goes with the other.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 19:6
precepts.why:
Peter calls us “a peculiar people”. What makes us peculiar? Wisdom answers: “For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them”. The peculiar commandments, the same thing Deuteronomy 4 said, are what separate us. They see the fringes on your garment. They see a beard on your face. They ask why y'all never come out with us on Saturday, and you say I have to keep the Sabbath. The Sabbath, what's that? I thought you said you was Christian. That is what separates you from everybody else.

The commandments “that were given unto them”: all these things were given only to us. That is why 1 Peter 2:9 is talking about the Israelites, not the white man. It is not white Grecians in togas, and the Galatians are not the white man in Turkmenistan. It is talking about you. So many of our brothers and sisters have been destroyed and don't see themselves as a prince, a ruler, a judge, but God says you are all of those things. All the leadership books go back to the Bible, which was given only to us, yet they make billions off leadership conferences while we sit at the bottom.

We must magnify the law: “The Lord is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law”. That is each and every one of our jobs, to put the laws of God on a pedestal and stand firm for them. When you do, it automatically puts you in a different position, different from everybody else on the face of the earth, because nobody else is standing firm for the commandments. The way you do anything is the way you do everything; nine times out of ten the cracker over you on the job is no better than you, but you are not doing things according to the commandments.

That separation shows. Our sisters dress modestly while the women in Houston dressed so out of order a dress code had to be put in place. Fifty men reading the Bible on a cruise become the disturbance. They make a man an offender for the word. But we were called out of darkness to show forth his praise. Nobody takes a light and puts it under a bushel, and you don't shine from the back. It is time for all of us to take our places.

thread.label: 1 Peter 3:3
thread.text: Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel;

classes.title: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.label: Sirach 36:23
precepts.why:
“Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel.” It is not saying a woman can’t have the outward adorning. Some think a woman has to look bummy and can’t get dressed up. Sisters can plait their heads and get fixed up; just don’t let your glory be in that, because a woman can be all hooked up and her spirit rotten. “But let it be the hidden man of the heart”, meaning Christ is in her spirit, “even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.”

What that hidden adorning sounds like, Sirach tells: “If there be kindness, meekness, and comfort, in her tongue, then is not her husband like other men.” A man who has a woman like this is not like most men, who don’t have it. That shows how rare this spirit is. Some brothers hear that verse and melt, because they don’t have it: do women like this even exist? Ask a sister and she can name twenty things she doesn’t like about her husband, but has to rack her brain for one or two good things.

Meek means obedience. Not always screaming, arguing and fighting, when the man just got through dealing with all that in the street and is the one making sure you have a house over your head and heat; you are biting the hand that feeds you. “For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord.” She adorned herself with subjection to her husband, and that is of great price, far above rubies. Not my lord on the phone with the sisters and cursing him as soon as the phone hangs up.

Beauty is corruptible, the clothes are corruptible; those things fade. A righteous spirit stays with you, and that is how you grow old in righteousness together watching the grandkids. Your inner spirit makes your outside look good. When you find a woman with kindness, meekness and comfort in her tongue, you will have paradise in your marriage and not a prison marriage, because husband and wife is the beginning, the nucleus of everything.

thread.label: 1 Peter 3:14
thread.text: But and if ye suffer for righteousness’ sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;

classes.title: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.label: Psalms 119:165
precepts.why:
Peter says, “But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye.” We must begin to learn how to suffer for righteousness' sake, for the sake of Christ. And we are happy in it: that happiness is our peace. Happy are they that keep God's laws.

David shows where that peace comes from: “Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” Nothing shall offend them means offenses, and being afraid of tribulation, will not make you turn your back on Christ.

That is why Peter goes on, “and be not afraid of their terror”: the terror of being persecuted. Times are not going to get easy, for husband, wife, brother or sister, so we have to prepare ourselves for hard and trying times and not go railing for railing with one another. Our best tools are praying, fasting, studying and increasing our faith, and following the instructions laid forth.

The man or woman who loves God's law has a peace the world cannot shake. When the tribulation comes, the law they love keeps them from being offended, and they endure it happy, suffering for righteousness' sake.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:1
precepts.why:
Peter laid out the instructions for marriages, because hard times are coming. thread.label: 2 Peter 2:18
thread.text: For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 2:4
precepts.why:
Paul warned of them: “by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” Good words and fair speeches: intellectual, big words, semantics, rhetoric. They serve theology; their theology is their god, and their own belly, money. Peter says the same: “For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh”. There are no laws involved, no commandments involved.

The commentary on Peter says it: false teachers who sound impressive yet deliver nothing of substance. Homoousios, hypostatic, exegesis, ontological, hermeneutical, Christological: great swelling words. Their speech is grand, polished, well paced, even spiritual sounding, like Bible, but it is hollow, with no commandments, no responsibility, no accountability. Unlike Paul, who said “my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power”. Paul refused persuasive words of man's wisdom; these teachers rely on style over truth, eloquence without gospel substance. In the Greek, great swelling words means great bulk: high sounding, but only words, vain and meaningless, with nothing but emptiness behind them.

Show me the scripture that says Christ is fully God and fully man. It isn't there. The word of God is plain and clear. Even their hermeneutics goes back to Schleiermacher, a German called the father of modern liberal theology, and Isaiah says “The vile person shall be no more called liberal”; the vile person will “utter error against the Lord, to make empty the soul of the hungry”. The word comes from Hermes, the Greek trickster god, so it is a trickster's interpretation, and the Jesuits carried it around the earth.

Peel back the swelling words and here is the premise: if Christ is fully God and fully man, only a two-essence being can keep God's laws, so we don't have to. But Christ said be perfect, as your Father in heaven is perfect, and Zacharias and Elisabeth walked “in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.” It can be done. “The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin”: their sport is not having to keep the commandments.

thread.text: And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you;

classes.title: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians
Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.label: Acts 26:22
precepts.why:
Peter says Paul wrote “according to the wisdom given unto him”, and wisdom is not a what but a who: Christ is the wisdom given to Paul. And Peter read “all his epistles”. He didn't say, this is off but I'll let it slide. If Paul wrote things that were off, that implicates Peter; if it implicates Peter it implicates James; and it implicates John, the last surviving disciple, who never wrote against Paul. You make Christ a negligent Messiah who sat quiet while Paul wrote error and then waited three thousand years to send somebody to fix it.

So what did Paul write from? “Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come”. When Paul crafted his letters, his primary reference was none other than what the prophets and Moses wrote. That is Paul's source material.

That is why Peter says the unlearned and unstable wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”: the law and the prophets. Wrest is short for wrestle; they twist Paul into saying what he did not say, because they don't really believe what the Bible says. The error of the wicked takes Paul's letters and says all nations can be saved, Paul grafted the nations in, we can commit adultery, the Sabbath is changed, we don't have to keep the laws anymore. Don't fall from your own stedfastness: Paul said none other things than Moses and the prophets.

precepts.label: Acts 28:23
precepts.why:
When they appointed Paul a day, many came to his lodging, “to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.” That is the other scriptures. His source material was the Old Testament.

Write this down: Paul's letters predate the gospels, with the exception of Mark. Mark, Luke and Matthew are the synoptic gospels, and it is said Matthew and Luke borrowed from Mark, because Mark was Peter's scribe. That is why Peter has no gospel: Mark is Peter's gospel, and it makes sense that it is the oldest, since Peter's and Paul's ministries were at the same time. Paul's letters range from the forties to the sixties AD. John was written around 90 AD, twenty years after Rome besieged Jerusalem in 70 AD, and Revelation around 95 to 100 AD.

So Paul was not pulling from John 3:16, because when he wrote his letters there was no John 3:16. He was not quoting John, Matthew or Luke; his letters came before them. Luke was travelling with him, and Luke wrote both Luke and Acts: Acts is basically a second Luke, Luke's letter number two.

That is why you cannot understand Paul's letters, the things hard to be understood, without the law and the prophets. Paul persuaded men concerning Jesus out of Moses and the prophets from morning till evening, and the unlearned who don't know those scriptures wrest Paul unto their own destruction.

precepts.label: Romans 1:7
precepts.why:
Peter says “our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you”. Peter is giving kudos and respect to Paul for the wisdom that was in him, and that wisdom is Christ, the spirit of Christ. But in Paul's epistles “are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest”. So first get clear on who Paul was writing to.

“To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.” Called to be saints. Who are the saints? Psalms 148 speaks of “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.” The children of Israel are the saints. We are the saints.

Some Christians say Paul was writing to Israelites and other nations at the same time. No. That is not who the letter is addressed to. It is addressed to the saints at Rome. Other nations are never referred to as saints. When you twist that and teach that your oppressor can be granted the same benefits as you, that the nations receive some twisted salvation, you have been “led away with the error of the wicked” and fallen from your own stedfastness. It is a whole different gospel, and that is how the unlearned wrest Paul unto their own destruction.

precepts.label: Romans 2:17
precepts.why:
Get some clarity on who Paul is writing to: “Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God”. Paul is writing to the Jews. There is obviously northern kingdom in the congregations too, but he is writing to Judah.

Romans 7 says the same: “Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,)”. Why does he speak to them that know the law? Because he is writing to Jews, “how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth”.

So Paul is writing to Jews, to those who know the law, to the saints at Rome. Is he addressing both Jews and Gentiles in the church? Yes, but the Gentiles there are the northern kingdom, and they are all saints. He is not writing to other nations at all.

That is why Peter says the unlearned wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”. They stumble because they think Paul was writing things out of thin air to all nations, when he was writing to Israel, men who rested in the law and boasted of God. Know who the letter is addressed to and much of what is hard to be understood in Paul becomes plain.

precepts.label: Revelation 2:9
precepts.why:
John “bare record of the word of God, and of the testimony of Jesus Christ, and of all things that he saw.” He saw things and he wrote them down. The testimony is what God gave the prophets: to Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Micah, Nahum, to Peter, Paul and the apostles. All the things these men wrote, the things that are going to happen to the children of Israel, is the testimony we as God’s witnesses are supposed to be speaking.

Here is one of those testimonies: “I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich)”. The real Jews are in a low state today. Then: “I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.”

That is what you are supposed to testify about. You have to identify the people that say they are Jews and are not, and say plainly: these people are not the people of God. Revelation 3:9 says it again: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet.”

When you read Revelation 2:9 and 3:9 on this earth, that is you testifying. We as God’s witnesses have to testify these things on the earth today.

precepts.label: Malachi 1:4
precepts.why:
“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”. Esau is going to rebuild. But “thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down”. When the Lord comes back he is going to destroy all the cities Esau built. This is the testimony God gave Malachi, the same kind of record John bare.

“And they shall call them”: the “they” are the witnesses, the prophets. We are the ones that call them “The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

So the testimony is to let the Caucasian race know that God hates them forever. That is you testifying; that is the law and the testimony. The prophets wrote it, John bare record of it, and God’s witnesses on this earth today speak it.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:10-11
precepts.why:
“Behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days”. They are going to pass laws to put us in prisons. That is why they keep building these detention facilities; they fill them with the people they call illegal aliens, but ultimately they are for the twelve tribes of Israel. Imagine ten days in a detention facility, being tortured, your wife and children or the brothers you war with slain in front of you, just to make you say you are not the twelve tribes and Christ is not black, and they will spare your life. Hell no. We have nothing to lose and everything to gain; they have no power over our souls.

Revelation 12 backs it up. We are going into Jacob’s trouble, when Esau does not want this gospel preached any further and will do whatever it takes to try to stop prophecy. “Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.” Our kingdom is soon to come; before then, we are accused day and night. That is the tribulation ten days, us losing our lives for this gospel.

“And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony”. Their testimony is the testimony of this gospel. Even when persecution happens we will not fold; we don’t care about any white Jesus or any doctrine outside the twelve tribes of Israel being redeemed from our oppressors, Babylon America.

“And they loved not their lives unto the death.” We cannot be trying to spare our lives when Jacob’s trouble takes off. Loving not your life unto death means resisting every temptation to go against your God and your people. Don’t be a damn traitor. That is being faithful unto death for the crown of life.

precepts.label: Romans 12:1
precepts.why:
“Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.” This is what we are going to sacrifice to get what is actually ours: eternal life, the kingdom of heaven.

Paul says it: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” Every time these prophets go out to teach the word, they are presenting their bodies a living sacrifice. All the prophets in the Bible did it, even unto death. John was banished to the isle of Patmos; James was beheaded. They were martyred because they understood the mission, and you brothers and sisters have to understand the mission. We are the true martyrs.

Many read “be thou faithful unto death” and do not understand it. You have to put yourself there and say: there is nothing these nations can do to me, nothing you can take from me, to make me turn and betray my eternal life. There is no resurrection for them.

“He that hath an ear, let him hear”: you have to be spiritual, keeping the commandments, to understand it. “He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death”, the death the Lord has power over, the death over your soul.

classes.title: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.label: Zechariah 4:11
precepts.why:
“What are these two olive trees upon the right side of the candlestick and upon the left side thereof?” Zechariah asks again about “these two olive branches which through the two golden pipes empty the golden oil out of themselves.” The oil is understanding. The answer: “These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth.”

The two anointed ones are the two witnesses. In Zechariah’s time they were Joshua the priest and Zerubbabel. Before Babylon it was Isaiah and Jeremiah; in Revelation 11 it is Moses and Elijah. Different names, different people, but the same pattern: God always sends his prophets forth in twos before he brings forth judgment.

That is why Christ sent the twelve and the seventy elders out two by two. You cannot make judgment without two witnesses. And when the witnesses come they bind and loose things on earth, they forgive and they condemn, because it is the Lord speaking through them.

The two witnesses also speak of Israel as a whole. God says his people are his witnesses; and there are the two sticks, the stick of Judah and the stick of Ephraim, the northern and southern kingdom. A witness has a testimony, and Israel is sent to testify on this earth before the judgment comes.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:18
precepts.why:
“For thy help will I send my servants”: God says he is going to send Isaiah and Jeremiah. And that is what happened. Isaiah and Jeremiah came and prophesied before Babylon came and destroyed Jerusalem.

That is the pattern behind “I will give power unto my two witnesses.” God always sends forth witnesses before he brings forth judgment, and he sends them in twos. Isaiah and Jeremiah before Babylon; Joshua and Zerubbabel in Zechariah’s day; Moses and Elijah in Revelation 11. Christ sent the apostles and the seventy out in twos for the same reason: you need two witnesses to bring forth judgment.

So the two witnesses of Revelation 11 are the two major prophets that come before the end, and they also speak of Israel as a whole, the people God calls his witnesses on this earth. Judgment does not fall until the witnesses have prophesied.

thread.label: Revelation 11:5
thread.text: And if any man will hurt them, fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies: and if any man will hurt them, he must in this manner be killed.

classes.title: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.label: Jeremiah 23:29
precepts.why:
What is the fire that proceeds out of the witnesses’ mouth? “Is not my word like as a fire? saith the Lord; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?” God’s word is like fire. That goes back to the same thing in Thessalonians: the wicked is consumed with the spirit of the Lord’s mouth.

So when “fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies”, it is the word of God coming out of the witnesses as they testify. As we teach the word of God, we are marking them for destruction, and every last one of our enemies is going to be destroyed with fire when Christ returns. “If any man will hurt them, he must in this manner be killed”: that is how they are going to die when Christ returns.

That is why Esau will try to kill the witnesses. He does not want judgment to come on him, and when the witnesses testify, judgment comes. As we teach his word, they are going to try to kill us, because they do not want us to testify.

The witnesses also “have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy”, to turn the waters to blood, “and to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will.” As often as they prophesy, the earth is smitten with plagues.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:17
precepts.why:
Read on in Revelation 11: “when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them.” That beast is Edom. After we finish testifying the laws and the testimonies, everything the prophets say, revealing who Edom is and who the synagogue of Satan is, judging everybody on the earth, they are going to kill us because of our testimony.

Revelation 12:17 says the same: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.” The dragon is Edom. He makes war with those of us that keep the commandments and are teaching the word of God, the laws and the testimonies.

Revelation 18 shows where: “Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her.” The apostles and prophets are here in America today, all twelve of them, teaching; and after they finish their testimony they will be killed. Before Babylon is destroyed most of them will be dead; the only one that might not be is John the Revelator. “And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth.” Her is Babylon, America, and they kill the prophets here because the prophets testify against them.

The whole earth is our courtroom. The gospel has to be taught throughout the whole world and then the end comes, because we are testifying against everyone: to wake up our people that are scattered, and to condemn the wicked.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:48-51
precepts.why:
“And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle”. Who is the eagle? The eagle was Rome at the time, and Rome is an extension of this place called America. Moses tells us about that eagle: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth”. That's Rome, when they came in and attacked us in Luke 21, the abomination of desolation of Matthew 24:15, when they destroyed us and ran us out of Jerusalem. From the end of the earth: from Europe.

“a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”: we did not understand their tongue when they landed here. Columbus found the Taino, a people who shared food, land and knowledge and fed him as an honored guest, and he wrote that they would make fine servants, and with fifty men he could make them do whatever he wanted. They knew what they came for. Within fifty years the Taino nation was virtually extinct. In Africa they sent explorers, missionaries with Bibles and the cross, and traders with gifts first; they ate at the tables of kings while mapping the gold and rubber, got treaties signed in crafty, ambiguous words, and at the Berlin conference of 1884 sat around a table and split up the continent. They came as swift as the eagle flieth. You can never trust that red man, that devil, that dragon.

“A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”: they didn't care about old or young; they put everybody to death and enslaved everybody. “And he shall eat the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy land, until thou be destroyed”, and leave neither “corn, wine, or oil, or the increase of thy kine”, kine being cattle, “until he have destroyed thee.”

Then the woman is nourished in her place, and that is America, where we've been nourished through their welfare system, their disability system, their politics, their religions, their educational and economic system. “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. Hungry, thirsty, needing clothing, a passport, a visa, a death certificate, anything we need, we have to go to them. “and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” The red man put a yoke of iron upon our necks, and we are destroyed today as a people. Even the ones speaking up for us say we love America: that is how destroyed we are.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:9
precepts.why:
The woman is nourished “from the face of the serpent.” Jump to verse 9 to see who the serpent is: “And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.”

That old serpent is the serpent from Genesis. He is called the Devil and Satan, and he deceived everybody; he deceived this whole world. He was cast out into the earth with his angels. That is who the face of the serpent is: the devil himself and his kids, the white man, the red man. They are the enemies Deuteronomy 28:48 says we serve, called the serpent in Revelation.

That is why verse 12 says “Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea! for the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time.” Woe means death and destruction; this earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He is mad right now, and that is why we are going through it.

And verse 15: “the serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the woman”. That flood is his media, his witchcraft, the same script read word for word on every station, the deceiving of the whole world coming out of the dragon's mouth. But “the earth helped the woman”: this Bible helps us understand what happened to us, what is happening now, and what is going to happen.

precepts.label: Amos 3:7
precepts.why:
“The temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven was opened”: everything the prophets wrote, the testimony, is opened, meaning we are understanding it and teaching it. Then “the seven angels came out of the temple, having the seven plagues”, and received “seven golden vials full of the wrath of God”, and a great voice said, “Go your ways, and pour out the vials of the wrath of God upon the earth.” The testimonies speak of the judgment and death that has to take place on the earth.

But before that can happen, something has to happen first. Amos reads: “Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey?” That is the lion we read in Ezra, roaring and chasing the eagle out of the wood. “Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid?” The trumpet is the witnesses, us teaching; when we testify, the people better be afraid. “Shall there be evil in a city, and the Lord hath not done it?” The Lord is behind it, through the angels with the seven last plagues.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” The prophets are his witnesses, and the secret he reveals to them is his testimonies. And when he reveals it to us, we are supposed to testify.

“The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord God hath spoken, who can but prophesy?” The lion roaring is Christ speaking to us, and we prophesy. “Publish in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt”: Ashdod is modern-day Tel Aviv in the land of Israel, and the land of Egypt is America. That is where we have to testify, and then the plagues are poured out.

thread.label: Revelation 18:4
thread.text: And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.

precepts.label: Isaiah 5:20
precepts.why:
“Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” What are we coming out of? What this society promotes: adultery, the music, murder, sodomy, homosexuality, drunkenness, drug abuse, idolatry, wicked entertainment and corruption. All the things God hates, against his laws, statutes and commandments, and all of it deceives us. We must expose this evil so you can learn how to save your own soul. Look at what they call the YNs: our people smoking, toting guns, women with guns bigger than they are, little kids holding bullets. And then they call us a hate group when we are trying to stop the evil within our own community first.

Sin is deceitful, and America has blurred the line. Your president even asks, what do you have to lose? Choose the worst of both evils. Isaiah 5:20: “Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!” Woe is destruction unto them. That is how they blur the line between good and evil.

Who does that? Your pastor. Many a black church on every corner facilitates the continuance of your oppression. So you have to choose a side: righteousness, your heritage, your nation, keeping God’s commandments.

That is the second step: study, pray, apply, see yourself in the scriptures, and then show your faith by separating yourself from evil. Our purpose is Acts 26:18: “To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God”. That is coming out of her.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 51:9
precepts.why:
Jeremiah speaks of Babylon: “We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed.” That is what they are trying to do now, in every aspect: heal America, just like the Bible says. Trump, make America great again, and all that. Listen, that is not going to happen. America is falling.

The Most High is showing it. America is about to celebrate its 250 years, and the front lawn of the White House looks shabby, the East Wing is under construction, the pool they spent all that money on is green with algae, and there is a fence around it all. When we were wicked in the world and had a birthday, we got a new outfit, a haircut, everything. Your 250th year should be something grandiose, and this is what your most pristine house looks like? Every picture shows it: a broken country. As in Daniel, the clay and the iron will never mix; everybody is going back to their own countries, and war is going to break out of this place.

Why can she not be healed? Because “her sins have reached unto heaven”. America made the biggest mistake of its life: it oppressed the children of Israel, the apple of God's eye, and even when we were supposed to be freed, it held forward the affliction and never opened the doors of its prisons. Because of her sins she keeps making the wrong decisions, hardening more and more towards us, and the Most High is taking note. There is a payment to pay, and no one can heal her.

thread.label: Revelation 19:12-13
thread.text: His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.

classes.title: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.label: Revelation 1:1
precepts.why:
“His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.” No man knew it but he himself, so what are you tripping about, YHWH, Yahawashi, Jesus Christ? We are English speakers; we learned Jesus Christ. Call him what you call him, but we have to keep the commandments.

“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.” Why is his vesture dipped in blood? Because Christ is about righteous destruction; you read that in Isaiah 63. The Lord is a man of war. We serve a terrible God, and a merciful one, and he is going to use these nations to create a final battle.

How do we know this is Jesus? Revelation 1:1: “The Revelation of Jesus Christ”. The whole book is the revelation of who? Jesus Christ. So the rider of Revelation 19, with eyes as a flame of fire, is Jesus Christ, and when he comes back he is not going to meet them as a man.

That is our hope: to see it and be part of it, the kingdom where all the wrongs done to us get turned upside down and right is instilled in the earth. Not a pie-in-the-sky fairy tale from modern-day Christianity, but Christ coming back to make war.

precepts.label: Revelation 1:14-15
precepts.why:
The same Christ of Revelation 19, whose “eyes were as a flame of fire”, is described in chapter 1: “His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire; And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace”.

Why his feet like fine brass, as if burned in a furnace? Because you cannot deny it anymore: Jesus Christ was a black man. The Bible says it first and foremost, and there is archaeological proof and historical evidence besides. Everyone knows it except the dumb Americans here in this country, and I say that because I was a dumb American; we were all dumb at one point. A lot of Eastern Europeans know Jesus was black. Vladimir Putin knows Jesus was black.

So this is who is coming: the black Christ whose eyes are like a flame of fire, his vesture dipped in blood. Jesus Christ is coming back to make war. Understand that now, as the wars are here and God is orchestrating every one of them from the beginning.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:11
precepts.why:
Ezra sees “a roaring lion chased out of the wood”, and he “sent out a man's voice unto the eagle”. The eagle is Rome, and Europe and America are the extension of it. The roaring lion is Christ, but first it is us, the prophets: a man's voice speaking to the eagle. That is the witnesses on the earth today condemning the so-called white man, Edom, for all the evil he has done through the centuries. God has not forgotten slavery, Jim Crow, the destruction of Jerusalem by Rome. He does not forget anything.

How will we overcome that beast? “And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.” We overcome the beast, Edom, by the blood of Christ, and by the word of our testimony.

What is our testimony? The words of the prophets. We are teaching the laws and the words of the prophets, revealing that he has ruled with deceit, set himself up as the Jews and the people of God, and dwelt on this earth “with much wicked oppression”. In a court of law the witnesses must bring their testimony before judgment comes, and the whole earth is our courtroom. When we speak, the Lord is speaking through us, the spirit of his mouth.

And by the blood of the Lamb, meaning Christ having mercy on us. If you make a mistake, fix it. If you are struggling with things inside, fix it. If you fall, get back up; Christ will have mercy on you. But you also have to have his testimony. That is how we overcome this wicked society, and then the eagle, its horrible wings, wicked feathers, malicious heads and hurtful claws, will appear no more.

thread.label: Judith 8:24
thread.text: Now therefore, O brethren, let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us, and the sanctuary, and the house, and the altar, rest upon us.

classes.title: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.label: Job 32:21-22
precepts.why:
“For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.” When you get the flattering title, your maker soon takes you away. What does that mean? You want the flattering title, you get the test, you fail the test. Bam. Thought I was worthy. Nope.

So be mindful of what you ask for. Brothers work underhandedly to become leaders, and it don't work like that; this is the Lord's business, and he is the one giving it out. Brothers that ask for rank, that say give me the 50's test, never make it, and that is how you know Satan is pushing them. When brothers ask for the test, nine times out of ten they fail it, because spiritually you are not ready if you are asking. Nobody asks to be a leader. The Lord raised all these men up. The Bishop didn't ask to be a bishop; he became a bishop. If you are asking for it, you are in the wrong place.

When the student is ready, the teacher will be there. The Lord will place you where you are supposed to be; promotion comes from the Lord, and there is a reason you are in the position you are in. Once you fulfill that office, the Lord will make it happen. Many brothers who wanted position fell down and never made it back, while others who were down came back on fire. The work determines where you are supposed to be. Brothers get jealous when another brother gets position, but if you love the Lord you work for the Lord, not for position. In Maccabees the brother who said let me get me a name ended up put to death.

That is what Judith 8:24 asks of a leader: not a title, but “let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us”. The higher up you go, the more people you serve. If you don't have the mindset to build up those beneath you and to support and push up the leader above you, forget it; the Lord can't use you.

thread.label: Wisdom of Solomon 1:5
thread.text: For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in.

classes.title: My Temple My Choice

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:11
precepts.why:
“For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in.” If you are deceitful, that holy spirit of discipline is not going to live with you, and it will not stick around when you are in sin.

Peter names the war: “Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”. That includes the lust for food. Overeating and snacking is a fleshly lust warring against your soul, and it drives out the spirit of discipline.

Thoughts “without understanding” are not knowing that we need you to do the work, so we need you healthy; your kids need you and you need yourself. So stop hating yourself and become disciplined. Fix your mind first and don’t say I can’t. Stop overeating, stop snacking, start fasting more, drink water instead of soda and juice, make exercise a lifestyle, eat light, and take care of your body.

Pray and fast that the Lord keeps your discipline. Ask him to change your appetite and strip away the cravings for sugar and processed carbs, and ask the Lord never to remove his holy spirit from you, so you can stay disciplined.
