thread.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:22-27
thread.text: For wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled, plain, not subject to hurt, loving the thing that is good quick,

classes.title: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.label: Mark 4:18-19
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:23 says wisdom is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care.” Free from what care? Free from worry and stress, and above all free from the cares of this world. Mark 4 names them.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of the world, the riches and the lusts of other things deceive you. Life does not consist in the abundance of things; they deceive you and choke the word.

Wisdom is free of those cares. The man that has wisdom is not going to be subject to the riches of this world. God said beware of covetousness, and that is wisdom, so I am going to beware of it; I am not going to entertain that.

So it is in our best interest to be paired with wisdom, because wisdom has “all power, overseeing all things.” Tether yourself to wisdom and you can see clearly, the cares of this world cannot choke the word, and it will not become unfruitful in you.

precepts.label: Hebrews 4:10-12
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 says wisdom is “the breath of the power of God.” What is the power of God? Hebrews 4 answers.

“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” We fought that example of unbelief. If we believe, we are tethered with God and following wisdom. Wisdom is pure, steadfast and sure, and we enter into that rest.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful.” Wisdom of Solomon 7:22 just said wisdom is “quick”, and “having all power.” The same words. And it is “sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.”

The intents of the heart are where sin begins. So we want that pure influence, so that the intents of this mind are not led astray and what guides and directs us is the word of God. There should be something in all of us that says, I can’t do that, it is wrong to do that. If we turn aside from that, we are saying we are hypocrites and don’t really believe. God has chosen us, for whatever reason, to give us wisdom. The power of God is the word of God. It is wisdom.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7-8
precepts.why:
Wisdom is “a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Influence means to mold you and direct you. If wisdom is flowing down from the Almighty and it is influencing you, you are connected, tethered, with God. Or something else can be influencing you, and that will not be wisdom; it will be covetousness, lust, whatever it might be. Psalms 19 shows what that pure influence is.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were once simple, but wisdom is now in us, making us wise. “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.”

That pure influence is the statutes, the laws of God. The commandment is “pure”, and it enlightens the eyes so that we can see clearly.

And if our eyes are enlightened and the Lord has converted us, what are we now? We are new, something different. That is where Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 goes: “remaining in herself, she maketh all things new.”

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 10:6
precepts.why:
Psalms 19 showed the law converting the soul, and once converted we are new. 1 Samuel 10:6 says the same thing: “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.”

With the word of God you change into another man. That is what Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 means: “she maketh all things new.” Wisdom will make you new, so you can’t keep doing the same thing.

But if the word is dealing with you and you are still trying to live that old man, still letting that old man tell you what to do, still doing that same stuff, the Lord says, I am going to beat you with many stripes, because I gave you something and you weren’t listening. Much is given, much is required. And don’t think many stripes is a pow pow and that is it. Many in that day will say “Lord, Lord”, and he is going to say, I don’t know you.

precepts.label: Luke 6:45-49
precepts.why:
“A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.” What comes out of his mouth is what is in him.

“And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” Why are you calling me Lord, Lord, and don’t do the things I tell you to do? “Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.” “But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell.”

The one built on Christ, which is the rock, is the one that is applying it. Applying it is the whole key. That is what strengthens the foundation and lets us endure when tribulations come. Wisdom teaches us that, and it is plain to understand. In that day men will say, Lord, Lord, did not I prophesy? Yes, but you still didn’t do what I told you to do. You were out on the street teaching, but you were a hypocrite; you weren’t living it.

Brothers sometimes come up wanting to understand the deep prophecies. Brother, let’s first help you get off of Pornhub. Why are you in Revelation trying to understand these archangels? You have to let that stuff go. You know prophecy, but you don’t know you yet. Learn you, so you are able to live it, and then instruct people wisely and teach them how to serve God.

precepts.label: James 1:27
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:26: “For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness.” Wisdom is unspotted. James 1:27 shows how a man keeps himself the same way.

“Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.”

You keep yourself unspotted from the world by visiting the fatherless and the afflicted, all people afflicted in the mind. But you are too busy trying to bag the chick. She came out of the world, out of whatever she was doing, and instead of leading her to God you are trying to sleep with her.

If we want to know how to keep ourselves unspotted, we tether ourselves to God, because flowing down from him is wisdom. You come into this truth not knowing any better, wisdom flows down from God to you, you apply it, and you become new: “she maketh all things new.”

precepts.label: Sirach 4:10
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 says wisdom, “in all ages entering into holy souls, she maketh them friends of God, and prophets.” Wisdom cannot dwell in a body that is subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness or hatred. Ecclesiasticus 4:10 shows the conversion of our minds in these last days: when we put our interests over the Lord’s, it distances us from him, and when we put the Lord’s interests over ours, it brings us closer to the heavenly Father.

“Be as a father unto the fatherless, and instead of an husband unto their mother.” That is the opposite of the mindset of a whoremonger, who asks, what can I do to this sister, how can I take advantage of this single mother? The son of the Most High asks, what can I do for this young man to build him up? That is why Bishop Nathanyel says it is easier to build up a young man, a child, than to fix a broken old man; the broken old man is the one looking to take advantage.

“So shalt thou be as the son of the most High.” If you go opposite of that, you cannot be the son of the Most High. If you are looking at this sister with lustful eyes, trying to figure out how to get in her pants or take advantage of her, you can’t be the son of the Most High, and wisdom cannot dwell in you.

That is the charge on the friend of God and the prophet: to go out and raise up God’s children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy. Much is given to you, and much is going to be required of you.

classes.title: Woe to Amerikkka

precepts.label: Ezekiel 35:5
precepts.why:
Wisdom says the Lord gave the ungodly “place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them”. Their malice is their hatred for us, shown in all the sins they have committed against us, and it is still going on: innocent blood shed again in Springfield, Illinois, a woman who called the police for help and ended up murdered in her own house. How do you call the police for help and they kill you?

Ezekiel names that malice: “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end”. While we are here struggling and suffering, they are still killing us.

That is why the Lord executes judgment on them “by little and little”: a flood here, a fire there, an earthquake here, a war there. He is not ignorant of what they are; he created them, so he knows their pedigree. “Their cogitation would never be changed”: their way of thinking, the hatred they have for us, cannot change. That is why the cop shot the man and said he did not even know why he shot him. It is in them.

It was there from the beginning: “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” He made up his mind from young to kill Jacob, and that thought has continued from generation to generation. It started with Cain and Abel, for Esau is Cain regenerated. That is the perpetual hatred.

“For it was a cursed seed from the beginning; neither didst thou for fear of any man give them pardon”. There is no pardon and no grace for Esau. His neck is on the chopping block, and the judgment coming to America will not change however much they jump, yell and shout. This land is Esau’s kingdom and we are just living in it, so do not set your affection on it.

thread.label: Sirach 3:3
thread.text: Whoso honoureth his father maketh an atonement for his sins:

classes.title: Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:9
precepts.why:
“Whoso honoureth his father maketh an atonement for his sins”, and that goes for your mother too. When you honour your father, that wipes away your sins. Hebrews shows why.

“Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence”. Another word for reverence is respect, honour. The fathers of our flesh corrected us and we gave them that honour.

“Shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?” So even more so we have to respect the Lord that created us. But that does not cancel the first part: we still have to have respect, honour and reverence for our earthly fathers. Thus saith the Lord. Honouring the father of your flesh is part of being in subjection to the Father of spirits, and that is why it makes an atonement.

precepts.label: Galatians 6:10
precepts.why:
Honouring your father and mother does not depend on whether they are a repentant Israelite or still in the world. You still have to respect and honour them either way.

We have to let our light shine and be the light to the Gentiles, the unrepentant of our people, because at one point you were unrepentant too. Paul says, “As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.” As much as the opportunity arises, we do good to all men, those in the truth and those out of the truth, and that includes the parents who raised us.

That goes back to Romans, where it says live peaceably with all men. So when Sirach says “Whoso honoureth his father maketh an atonement for his sins”, it is not only the father who is in the faith; doing good to your parents wherever they stand is the honour that brings that atonement.

thread.label: Sirach 3:3-4
thread.text: Whoso honoureth his father maketh an atonement for his sins:

classes.title: Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.label: Matthew 6:19-20
precepts.why:
Sirach says “he that honoureth his mother is as one that layeth up treasure.” We are not talking about gold or diamonds or crypto or NFTs. Christ shows what kind of treasure it is.

“Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal”. The treasures on earth, crypto coins and Bitcoin, can go when the computers blow up; money is going to burn; gold can melt; somebody can steal it.

“But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal”. The treasure in heaven is the eternal life we are all striving for. Nothing can take that away from us once we attain it, and no thief can break through and get what the Lord has prepared for us in paradise.

So honouring and respecting your mother is laying up that treasure in heaven. But we have got to get there.

thread.label: Sirach 3:5
thread.text: Whoso honoureth his father shall have joy of his own children; and when he maketh his prayer, he shall be heard.

classes.title: Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.label: John 9:31
precepts.why:
“Whoso honoureth his father shall have joy of his own children; and when he maketh his prayer, he shall be heard.” Why does it say that? It means that when you are not honouring your father or your mother, your prayers are not going to be heard, which shows that honouring your parents is a commandment.

John makes it clear and plain: “Now we know that God heareth not sinners”. Everybody knows it. Dishonouring your parents is breaking a commandment, and a sinner is not heard.

So when we are in habitual, presumptuous sin, the Lord is not going to hear our prayers. The one who honours his father is keeping the commandment, and that is why, when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard.

thread.label: Sirach 3:7
thread.text: He that feareth the Lord will honour his father, and will do service unto his parents, as to his masters.

classes.title: Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.label: Hebrews 13:17
precepts.why:
“He that feareth the Lord will honour his father, and will do service unto his parents, as to his masters.” The same respect you have for your boss, your employer, whoever gainfully employs you, the elders and the men over you, you should have for your parents and more, because they brought you into this world.

Hebrews says it plain and simple: “Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls”. These people watch for our souls.

Your parents did that too. Even in the past, before they or you knew the truth, they watched out for your life, your safety and your well-being. They cared for you all the way up to the time you were able to repent and become a commandment-keeping Israelite. So have respect and honour for them, and do service unto them as to your masters.

thread.label: Sirach 3:8-9
thread.text: Honour thy father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon thee from them.

classes.title: Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.label: Proverbs 13:22
precepts.why:
“Honour thy father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon thee from them.” Both in word and deed means whatever you say, do it. The blessing comes from them, and “the blessing of the father establisheth the houses of children.” How can the blessing of a father establish children? Solomon shows it: “A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children.”

Children's children are grandchildren. So if you have a good relationship with your family, with your mother and your parents, you never know: they could be saving money for your children, for their college tuition. They could be leaving that blessing for you just because of the way you conduct yourself and the way you treated them with respect.

But you only get that blessing if you are honouring and respecting your parents and doing what the Lord says to do. If you are acting up and being disrespectful to them, and not letting your light shine as an Israelite should, they are not going to deal with you, and you will never even see it. They are not going to help you with the baby when stuff comes. They are not going to help you get that stroller. They are not going to wash the kids for you. They are not going to do none of those things if you are not honouring and reverencing them.

That is how the father's blessing establishes the houses of children: honour him in word and deed, and his inheritance reaches down to your own children.

thread.label: Sirach 3:9
thread.text: For the blessing of the father establisheth the houses of children; but the curse of the mother rooteth out foundations.

thread.label: Sirach 3:10-11
thread.text: Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father’s dishonour is no glory unto thee.

classes.title: Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.label: Proverbs 17:6
precepts.why:
“Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father’s dishonour is no glory unto thee.” Oh, my dad, yeah man, he is broke, he is a bum now, my mom left him behind. That is no glory to you. You came from him. “For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father.” Solomon says the same: “Children’s children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.”

Children's children, the grandchildren, and the great-grandkids are the crown of old men. They want to see you have children and keep procreating. They see it and say, dang, you came from me, and now you are creating life again. Man, I would love to see that. Parents love seeing that.

And the glory of children are their fathers. So if your father is in dishonour, you are in dishonour too. There is no glory in that, and “a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.” The honour of the parents and the honour of the children are tied together, one generation to the next.

That is why we have got to let our light shine: so our fathers are honoured in us, and we become a crown to them.

thread.label: Sirach 3:12-16
thread.text: My son, help thy father in his age, and grieve him not as long as he liveth.

classes.title: Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.label: Jeremiah 2:33
precepts.why:
Sirach warns that “he that angereth his mother is cursed: of God.” Does that mean you are in sin because your mom is mad you are not coming to the Christmas party, or because you did not come over for Mother’s Day with a bouquet of flowers? Jeremiah answers it.

“Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love?” We cannot trim our ways in keeping the commandments to seek love, affection and acceptance from our family members.

“Therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways.” When we do that, we teach our family members to be wicked. We say we are not going to do this or that, then they say, come do this with us, and we cave in. That shows them we are not really about the word of God.

So honouring your parents is helping your father in his age, having patience with him when his understanding fails, not despising him when you are in your full strength. It is not trimming the commandments to keep the peace at their holidays.

thread.label: Sirach 12:10
thread.text: Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.

classes.title: 2025 Recap: Different Times, Same Truth

precepts.label: Isaiah 28:15
precepts.why:
“Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” That sounds harsh, but it is in the Bible. We had DEI and the Civil Rights Act since 1964, and y’all thought y’all were good. Then Trump rolled it back, and Walmart, Meta, Amazon, McDonald’s all followed, every last one of them in agreement. And y’all act surprised. This is the same man who sent the National Guard so you couldn’t go to school with him, bombed little girls in a church, and bombed the all-black Wall Street. You think he loves you now? His wickedness rusts back through like iron.

Then a black man in a suit and tie on national television said that when Americans see deportations and the border closed, they will say, this is what I voted for, and Daddy’s back. The black man is in love with his oppressor; that is why we can’t win our people over. Y’all thought Diddy was bad. The white race as a collective is the real Diddy.

Isaiah names that spirit: “Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves.”

That is what you just saw. Because he has a little higher position in captivity than his brothers, he makes lies his refuge and thinks the scourge will not come to him. A grown man calling the white man daddy: how is a black woman going to respect you after that? He made a covenant with death and hell, trusting the enemy that the Bible says never to trust.

precepts.label: John 19:15
precepts.why:
“Never trust thine enemy.” Yet our people cheer for him. When TikTok was brought back and they gave Trump the credit, social media was full of people playing Dear Mama, a song near and dear to our hearts, to commemorate Donald Trump. It shows how near and dear the white man is to their heart. They are happy he will allow them their debauchery.

John shows the same spirit in Christ’s day: “But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him.” Get rid of the black Messiah, the righteous man. “Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King?” And what did the black bourgeoisie of that day say? “The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar.”

Daddy’s home. That is the Daddy in the scriptures. The chief priests rejected their own King and claimed Caesar, just as our people today reject the truth and call the white man daddy.

Then they act confused when he shows his true colors and rolls back DEI. You knew it was a snake. That is what Christianity does: you never read the Bible, you are put to sleep every week, and when you go out in the world everybody sees color except you. Open your Bible. Never trust thine enemy.

thread.label: Sirach 15:15
thread.text: If thou wilt, to keep the commandments, and to perform acceptable faithfulness.

classes.title: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.label: Sirach 19:20
precepts.why:
Sirach 15:15 says, “If thou wilt, to keep the commandments, and to perform acceptable faithfulness.” Keeping God's commandments is performing acceptable faithfulness: those are your actions, and that is where your faith lies. Your works prove your faith and your faith proves your works; they go hand in hand. God “hath set fire and water before thee: stretch forth thy hand unto whether thou wilt.”

For anyone still confused, Sirach 19:20 says it again: “The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.” The performance of the law is the acceptable faithfulness of Sirach 15. Wisdom is not only knowing the law; it is performing it.

The words “the knowledge of his omnipotency” mean knowing that God is all around us, and we acknowledge it by keeping his laws.

This is what Habakkuk and Paul mean by the just living by faith. Paul says “the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The just are those who keep God's laws and commandments, and they live by faith in Christ. Fearing God, keeping his law and living by faith are one walk.

precepts.label: Genesis 26:5
precepts.why:
God told Isaac why the promise stood: “Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” Abraham obeyed, and he kept the charge, the commandments, the statutes and the laws. That is past tense. It tells you what Abraham was doing from the beginning that proved his faith. His obedience was his acceptable faithfulness, the performance of Sirach 15:15.

Paul writes, “And the law is not of faith: but, The man that doeth them shall live in them.” The law meant there is the law of sacrifice, which came later. Abraham's faith came first, and his faith and the promise to him go hand in hand; the promise predates the law of sacrifice.

“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us”. The curse of the law is condemnation, not being able to atone for every sin. Caiaphas pointed it out without knowing it: “it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” Both the northern and southern kingdoms were under the old covenant they agreed to in Deuteronomy 27 and kept breaking, so both were condemned and destroyed by the nations. But the Lord loved them, sent his son to die for them, and took them out of that contract into a new one, “That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ”, meaning the northern kingdom.

Paul says “before faith came, we were kept under the law”, and “the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.” The schoolmaster is the law of sacrifice, and the “we” is Israel. After faith came, “we are no longer under a schoolmaster.” Jews, Greeks, bond, free, male and female were all the same people of God in Christ.

“And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.” Abraham is the father of faith, so his children should be children of faith like him: keeping the commandments the way he did, with faith in Christ instead of the animal sacrifice the Galatians were bewitched back into. The promise pertains to the Israelites, not to all nations.

precepts.label: Matthew 1:21
precepts.why:
A well-respected black theologian, preaching before white people all over the place, taught that race is a social construct and not a biblical concept. False. The Bible is the family tree; Genesis 10 is the table of nations. Sirach says: “My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers”: keep your seed, your nobility, your race, and don’t pollute it with other nations. “When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field”, find your wife, “sow it with thine own seed, trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” Seed and race are the same thing. “So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” So what is he talking about? These pastors don’t know the Bible, and he never opened it once.

Matthew shows who Christ came for: “And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” His people. You go to somebody’s house and they say, that’s his people: that means his family, his kinfolk. The Bible was written by black people, and kindred and kinfolk are all in it.

Christ came to save his own race. He never came for any other race or nation. That is why the old family Bibles had the whole lineage written in them.

Yes, we all come from Adam, but Ezra makes the difference: of Adam come we all, “And the people also whom thou hast chosen.” As for the other people which also come of Adam, “thou hast said that they are nothing.” God chose a people out of Adam, and those are the people Christ came to save from their sins. Time is up on the Christian church.

precepts.label: Sirach 38:15
precepts.why:
“For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.” That belly ache late at night, that belly pain: you are sick. “By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.” The Bible says if you keep overeating, you are going to die. So I guess the Bible is a bully’s book? No. You just hate God and you hate yourself, because loving God is the only way to love yourself. When the white man’s own Department of Health says eight Swedish fish is past a child’s safe arsenic level, you say nothing; when we tell you to stop eating junk, it’s bullying. If you call it bullying, you will not take heed, and you will live a very short life. That is what the Bible says, not what I say.

Then Sirach says: “He that sinneth before his Maker, let him fall into the hand of the physician.” What will make you get sick and fall into the hand of the physician? Overeating. The Bible says, if you want to live long, don’t do it. But do we take heed? No, we don’t.

Fat does not stay harmlessly under the skin. Visceral fat wraps around the heart, the lungs, the liver, the stomach and the intestines, and makes your organs work double time, so you always feel weak, tired, low on energy. You don’t feel pain, so you don’t think it’s happening, until one day, bam, stroke; bam, heart attack; high cholesterol, heart bypass surgery. Eating sugar and overeating, you walk around like a ticking time bomb.

That is what we are trying to prevent: you ending up in a hospital bed, in the physician’s hand, because you sinned against your Maker with your mouth. Take heed to what is written, and prolong your life.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 15:9-17
precepts.why:
Sirach says “Let us now praise famous men” and names them as “Leaders of the people”, leaders, not one. Second Maccabees shows what those leaders do. Judas Maccabeus was preparing the men for war, and we are at war too, brothers: against sin and against our physical enemies, the children of Satan, Edom, Esau.

First a leader has to know the condition of the battle. “And so comforting them out of the law and the prophets, and withal putting them in mind of the battles that they won afore, he made them more cheerful.” If the first time you hear there is a war going on is weeks after it started, you are sleep. If you are not comforting yourself, your children, your wife and your husband out of the law and the prophets, you are not ready for the famine the Lord said is coming, when your stomach touches your back and your kids are looking at you.

“And when he had stirred up their minds, he gave them their charge, shewing them therewithal the falsehood of the heathen, and the breach of oaths.” That is why the class keeps showing that Esau is the devil, lying and breaking every treaty and oath. If your daughter secretly wants to be Tinkerbell, or wears the Frozen wig because she thinks Esau is still a princess, she does not see his breach of oaths. As a mother and a father you have to rework her mind and put her in the mindset of our fathers. Keep the body, take the mind: that was the slave master’s method, and the leader’s work is to take back the mind.

“And this was his vision”: leaders are visionaries, and where there is no vision the people perish. Onias was “a virtuous and a good man”; virtue is moral excellence, and our moral compass is God’s commandments that make us shine like gold. He was “reverend in conversation”, eloquent in speech; “gentle in condition”, keeping his composure, not hot-headed; “well spoken also”; and “exercised from a child in all points of virtue.” Nobody wakes up leading people. We are born leaders, but we become that in time. And “holding up his hands prayed for the whole body of the Jews”: leaders serve and sacrifice themselves for the betterment of the people.

Jeremias gave Judas a sword of gold: “Take this holy sword, a gift from God, with the which thou shalt wound the adversaries.” Then “Thus being well comforted by the words of Judas”: not Judas’s own mindset but the words of God, which comfort a people with a spirit of fear on them and stir them up “to valour, and to encourage the hearts of the young men.” They determined “courageously to set upon them, and manfully to try the matter by conflict.” That is the result of a great leader.

That is why the nations destroy the leaders first, because the leaders are in many cases the lifeline of the people. A leader is needed to bring comfort to a people that has been robbed, raped and murdered, and no nation on this planet needs great leaders more than ours.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 3:43
precepts.why:
Sirach praises the “Leaders of the people”, plural, and First Maccabees shows how they worked: “They said one to another, Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” They said it one to another. Nobody tried to do it by himself. When the Bishop went to the streets, he had a reader; that is why the scriptures say go two by two. The Bishop has said for years that this work is too big for one man.

We are in that decayed estate now. The mindset of 99% of our people is in a horrible state: our women thinking they can wear tights outside and nothing is wrong, grown men going outside in a crop top with the belly out, our young women on the dance teams. If that does not put you in a different state of mind, you are destroyed. That is the urgency you see in the brothers teaching loud in the streets, and that is why the Bishop and the deacons teach the way they teach.

Restoring the decayed estate of our people is what is happening at IUSC: our women in order, our men in order, our children in order.

“Let us fight for our people”, and for the sanctuary. You will go way further for somebody else than you will for yourself, and sacrifice way more for someone else than for yourself. That is why selfish people only go so far: they are satisfied at some point. A leader’s mind is on the whole people, like the leaders Sirach praises, who left a name behind them.

precepts.label: Psalms 51:3-13
precepts.why:
Sirach says of David, “In all his works he praised the Holy One most high with words of glory; with his whole heart he sung songs, and loved him that made him.” But didn't David sin against God? He did. Yet “The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” David sinned, but David repented, and God took away his sins.

This is how he repented: “For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me. Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.” He confessed.

“Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.” And after he confessed, what did David do? “Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” Get myself right, and then I'm going to go teach the people.

He teaches them “That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.” Look at my example: it is good to follow the Lord, because in the end the Lord chose me as his friend.

David is a famous man, and he is an example for all of us. Some of us err in this truth, but you can recover yourself and still earn a name. You just have to do the work and be sincere. Much is given and much is required of us as leaders, so we have to be honest, confess, get clean, and then lead the people back to God.

precepts.label: Baruch 4:1-4
precepts.why:
Sirach ends the praise of Elias and Eliseus with the people after them: “Of whom some did that which was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sins.” So what is pleasing to God? Baruch answers it: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.”

Then: “O Israel, happy are we: for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us.” The things pleasing to God are his laws. Us keeping the law is what pleases God. So when Sirach says some did that which was pleasing to God, it means some did the laws of God, and the rest multiplied sins.

That ties back to verse 10, where Elias was “ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the Lord’s judgment, before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.” That is our job, before it breaks forth, before the decree brings forth and the fierce anger of God comes, as Zephaniah 3 says: to turn our people back to God.

What is well pleasing to God is for us to keep his laws first, and then become the prophets that lead the people back to them. Much is given, much is required of us in our walk as leaders.

precepts.label: Sirach 50:1
precepts.why:
After Josias, the twelve prophets, Zorobabel, Neemias and Joseph, Sirach carries the line of renowned men on to the priesthood: “Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again, and in his days fortified the temple”. Simon repaired the house again. Like Neemias, “who raised up for us the walls that were fallen, and set up the gates and the bars, and raised up our ruins again”, his name is tied to building back what was broken down.

That is how these renowned men earned their names. It was about building back, walking in integrity, moving right. Josias “behaved himself uprightly in the conversion of the people”, not using his position to take advantage of the people or handling the word of God deceitfully. Neemias raised the walls and established the laws again, so nobody would come in trying to get our people to shop on the Sabbath. Simon repaired and fortified the house of God.

So it is with us: “in the time of the ungodly he established the worship of God.” In the midst of all this debauchery we are to establish the worship of God, with no hypocrisy, no covetousness and no murmuring, so that the people see us and say these are those guys we heard about that are going to come back on the earth. That is how you become the famous man.

The class only jumped through these chapters for time’s sake. Go through Sirach 44 to 50 again on your own, because there is a lot more in them.

precepts.why:
Baruch says, “Thus we were cast down, and not exalted, because we have sinned against the Lord our God”, and “unto us and to our fathers open shame, as appeareth this day.” Here in America we have open shame, because we departed from our God and refuse to come back and repent. “All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem.” All the other nations pass by and clap their hands at us. They are happy we are thrown down, happy we are not exalted, happy we are at the bottom.

“Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?” Everybody knows we are the perfection of beauty: our skin, our hair, our lips, our eyes. Flip the coin and look at Esau, wrinkled and dried up with skin cancer, twenty years old looking forty. And we are the joy of the whole earth: even in the lowest state we are in, everything we do, everybody follows.

“All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they hiss and gnash the teeth.” Starting with Edom on down. You go in the Chinese hair store, the nail shop, the gas station, the Arab store, the East Indian store, and they open their mouth against you; they don’t give a damn about you. “They say, We have swallowed her up: certainly this is the day that we looked for; we have found, we have seen it.” We don’t have a community, only neighborhoods, and in our own neighborhoods they own everything and we are the consumers. This is the day they hoped for, to see us break our laws and fall.

But now the Lord is waking his prophets back up to get his people back in order, to turn this place upside down, so we can have rulership on this earth again in righteousness.

precepts.label: Proverbs 21:16
precepts.why:
Baruch says the law “endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Since the beginning of time this law has been in place. Break it and judgments come upon you; keep it and blessings come upon you. Solomon shows what happens to those who leave it: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”

Look at your old pictures and old videos from when you were in the world. You look dead, spiritually dead. Run down and tired, twenty-one years old looking forty, when that was supposed to be the pinnacle of life, of your youth. We wandered out of the way of understanding, and we were like the walking dead. That is why the law is called a spirit: the commandments are spirit, and without them there is no life in us.

They make those movies mocking us. We were the congregation of the dead. And it is ironic that zombies walk groping. That is groping at noonday, what the Lord said would come on us for breaking his commandments: walking around trying to catch on to something, gravitate to something, all confused in the spirit. Even with the sun at its apex we could not see. We were blinded. We were distracted.

So the law is the difference between the living and the dead. Those who keep it come to life, the way we did when we came into this truth; those who wander from it remain in the congregation of the dead.

precepts.why:
“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. classes.title: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 9:16-17
precepts.why:
The prayer is that God would “give you all an heart to serve him, and to do his will, with a good courage and a willing mind.” If you want to return, if you want to repent, he will give you a heart to serve him and to keep his law and commandments. And it must be with a willing mind. Paul shows what that means.

“For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of”: though we preach the gospel, we have nothing to glory of, because all the glory goes back to the Father. “For necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!” Necessity is laid upon each and every one of us to go out there and wake our people up, so they can repent, come out of it, and cast away their iniquities. Woe unto us if we preach not the gospel.

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward.” We have to do this thing willingly. Nobody can force you. If you do it willingly you have a reward: a crown, everlasting life, immortality. “But if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me.” If you do it against your will, he will take his spirit from you, and you will find yourself back outside those doors in the midst of wickedness and evil again.

So we have to serve the Lord with a willing mind, a sincere heart, and loyalty. We have to come out of all the wickedness we learned here in America, from under the hypnosis given to us here, and serve him willingly.

precepts.label: Isaiah 59:1-2
precepts.why:
The prayer asks God to “send you peace, And hear your prayers, and be at one with you, and never forsake you in time of trouble.” You wonder why you have no peace in your life right now, why you are all over the place? Because you are not serving him, not keeping his law and commandments in sincerity. Isaiah shows what keeps us from being one with God.

“Behold, the Lord’s hand is not shortened, that it cannot save.” His hand is not so short that he can’t reach down and help you when you are afflicted or in trouble. “Neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear.” His ear is not so heavy that he can’t hear your prayers and your cries and come down and get you out of that situation.

“But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.” That is what separates you from your God: your sins, your iniquities. That is the only way he separates himself from you, if you are in the midst of sin.

But if you are doing what you are supposed to do, keeping the law of commandments in the faith of Christ, he is going to come to you, send you peace, and hear your prayers. If you are sincere and honest with him, walking right in his sight, waking up and returning to him, he will never forsake you in time of trouble. He will help you through your hard times.

precepts.label: Psalms 96:5
precepts.why:
The third brother, when they came to cut him, put out his tongue right away and held forth his hands manfully: come on, let's get this over with. He said courageously, “These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.” And “the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man's courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.”

Why did they marvel? They had to understand there was a certain spirit in these brothers; there was something the brothers knew that the king did not. The psalm tells what it is: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

All the gods of the nations are idols, so the nations have no living God. The king had power, arrogance and the fire, but his gods were dead. These brothers served the Lord that made the heavens, the God who gave them their tongues and hands and would give them again. That is why they were ready to die rather than transgress the laws of their fathers, and why the heathen could only stand there and marvel.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 8:5-6
precepts.why:
The king marveled at the young man's courage, and Paul shows the reason. “For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,) But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.”

Because we understand that there is only one living God, that is why they marvel. That is why the king was marveling. The nations have gods many and lords many, but a man who knows the one God, the Father, and the one Lord Jesus Christ can say, “we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers.”

Do you know what level of faith that is? You truly cannot desire anything left in this world. We are already captives: you have bills, you work fourteen hours a day. What are you leaving? There has to be something better. So the brothers went to the fire expecting “the King of the world” to raise them up “unto everlasting life”, and the fourth told the king, “as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.”

That hope belongs to those who have the one God. What kind of mercy would it be for the same people that torment us to get an equal reward in the kingdom? That is not a merciful God. The one God of Israel will of his own mercy give his servants breath and life again.

classes.title: The God Of War & Salvation

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 18:7
precepts.why:
The brother about to die said, “It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him.” It is good that this mortal body is slain when you look for a resurrection from the Almighty. “As for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life”: as for the heathen, the fake Jews, the Iranians, the other nations, there is no resurrection for them. There is a difference between the twelve tribes of Israel and the other nations. The Most High made a covenant with our forefathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

Wisdom of Solomon goes along with it, and this has to be your mindset concerning salvation and gathering with your people: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of those who are against you come together.

So don’t get scared, y’all. Don’t be scared when you see your enemies’ blood being shed. Maybe some blood might splatter on you. Don’t get scared. The Lord has got our back, and we will not fear what man can do to us: you can kill this body, and we look to be raised again.

Until we receive our homeland, we are all we got. We are pilgrims here, with no favorite place, only our favorite people, the faithful brothers and sisters who keep the commandments. So we must keep the unity, show ourselves friendly, exhort each other, and show charity and mercy one to another.
